ranked.name: OLIVO x BACTROCERA OLEAE x TOSCANA (AgroAmbiente.info, crop=2, survey_schema=1 'Infestazione mosca dell'olivo')
ranked.region: Toscana (11 provinces; Arezzo, Firenze, Grosseto, Livorno, Lucca, Pisa, Pistoia, Prato, Siena, Massa-Carrara)
ranked.outcome_type: PERCENTAGE (true rate over a fixed known denominator: tot=100 destructively sampled olives per visit; underlying per-stage COUNTs also served — u, l1v/l1m, l2v/l2m, l3v/l3m, pv/pm, fu — with server-computed totale/dannosa/attiva)
ranked.panel_stability: ROTATING BUT RECONSTRUCTABLE. Skeptic reproduced the hunter exactly: 39 id_field values present in all 7 verified years; adjacent-year overlap decays 261 -> 222 -> 188 -> 143 -> 126 -> 102. Stable id_field + name + lat/lon per grove means a panel can be rebuilt rather than assumed. Season volume corrected downward to ~4,006 rows/year (full 2024 week sweep, w23-w42), so realistic corpus is ~28k rows over 2020-2026, not the hunter's speculative ~40k/yr.
ranked.geographic_resolution: Point lat/lon (WGS84) per grove + ISTAT comune code, comune name, sub-area and province
ranked.defence_data: YES, and the strongest verified in the whole set after the incumbent itself. difesa is a working per-record stratifier (skeptic: difesa=bio returned 56 of 294 rows for 2024 w36), and survey_schema=3 'Trattamenti' carries data_ultimo_tratt. + tipo_trattamento (real but thin: 11 rows in the week sampled). CAVEAT the hunter got wrong and the skeptic caught: user_access is a SILENT NO-OP — all/validated/not_validated/test all return exactly 294 rows for 2024 w36, so test and unvalidated grower-entered records CANNOT be excluded server-side.
ranked.adama_relevance: Olive fly is a real ADAMA Italy insecticide market, and this sits on the IDENTICAL API, identical data model and identical auth-free access path as the incumbent Toscana Vite x Peronospora source — marginal engineering cost is close to zero for a team already harvesting crop=3. It does NOT exercise fungal epidemiology and cannot substitute for a Plasmopara backtest; that is a hard relevance ceiling, not a data defect.
ranked.backtest_potential: HIGHEST of any surviving candidate on measurement quality. The denominator is known and fixed (n=100 fruit), so the outcome is a calibratable, weightable rate rather than an ordinal band — you can compute Brier scores and reliability curves, not just rank correlations. A second independent numeric outcome on the SAME grove network exists (survey_schema=71, pheromone catture, 636 rows verified across 2021/2023/2025), giving a cheap cross-check. Weekly cadence + point coordinates make an ARPA/LaMMA Toscana agrometeo join straightforward in shape (NOT executed by either agent, so 'feasible' is a judgement on data shape, not a verified join). Hard ceiling: 2006-2019 is ACCESS_FAILED (server SQL type-cast bug on the plus_images join, confirmed on 5 separate pre-2020 years), so usable history is 2020-2026 only.
ranked.why_this_rank: I re-fetched it myself this session: HTTP 200, data.ok=true, rowCount=294, len(data)=294, verbatim val {"tot":"100",...,"totale":0.0,"dannosa":0.0,"attiva":0.0} — real rows, not a 200-with-zero-rows mirage. The skeptic attacked it hardest on observation-vs-model and FAILED: he pulled the server's own calculated_field SQL and it is plain arithmetic over stages a technician physically dissected out of 100 olives (totale = ((u+l1v+l1m+l2v+l2m+l3v+l3m+pm+pv+fu)/tot)*100), with no degree-day, no risk index, no 'condizioni favorevoli'. It ranks first because it is the only surviving Italian series that combines a measured rate with a known denominator, a working defence-regime stratifier, 7 verified years, ~28k rows, point geolocation, weekly cadence and near-zero integration cost. It is beaten on crop relevance by the vine candidates below and I do not pretend otherwise.

ranked.name: VITE x LOBESIA BOTRANA (tignoletta) x ABRUZZO (AgroAmbiente Abruzzo, crop=3, survey_schema=5)
ranked.outcome_type: COUNT (media_catture = mean adult catches per pheromone trap per reading; secondary ordinal INCIDENCE variable percentuale_infestazione, code table resolved by the skeptic: 34 nessuna, 1528 non rilevata, 1317 <5%, 1318 5-10%, 1319 10-15%, 1320 15-20%, 1321 20-50%, 1366 >50%)
ranked.panel_stability: TWO DISJOINT ERAS, not one 7-year panel. Skeptic measured id_field overlaps: 2020-21=28, 2021-22=30, 2024-25=34, 2025-26=37, but 2022<->2024 share only 2 fields. Zero fields appear in all six populated years. Longest usable stable panel = 3 consecutive seasons (27 fields, 2024-2026; 14 fields, 2020-2022). 2023 is a verified platform-wide hole (27 records, 5 fields) — probed across schemas 5, 7 and 4 and confirmed a real data gap, not ACCESS_FAILED.
ranked.geographic_resolution: Point lat/lon per vineyard field (162 distinct coordinate pairs, 166 id_field) + comune, monitoring area, province
ranked.defence_data: PRESENT BUT NEARLY EMPTY, and this is the single largest threat to its use. Only 85 of 3,530 rows carry a prodotto and 58 a treatment date (97.6% unobserved). Critically, 'confusione sessuale' (mating disruption, code 261) is one of the product options — where deployed, pheromone-trap catches are structurally suppressed and stop tracking population, and since prodotto is blank on almost every row this intervention is not identifiable.
ranked.adama_relevance: Vine, in an ADAMA Italy market region, on the exact decision (insecticide/BT timing against Lobesia generations) that a disease-intelligence advisory would try to sharpen. Same 'aedita' platform family as the incumbent, so the harvester is a near copy.
ranked.backtest_potential: The best VINE numeric series with genuine variance in the whole set. 3,424 of 3,530 rows carry a numeric media_catture and 1,733 are strictly >0 (range 0-200), so it is not a wall of zeros. Weekly, point-geolocated, therefore directly joinable to regional agrometeo for a degree-day / flight-phenology backtest. The skeptic independently computed the 2025 weekly mean-catch curve and got a clean three-generation flight signature (wk15-18 first flight 2.6-4.3, trough wk20-23 at 0.1-0.3, wk24-28 second flight 2.0-6.4, wk31-34 third peaking 13.6, zero by wk38) — noisy and site-heterogeneous in the way real voluntary field data is, not a smooth generator. Honest limits: media_catture is pre-averaged with an unexposed denominator (trap count, days since servicing), so a per-site random effect is mandatory; a missing week is not a zero catch; and median 11 readings per field-year means 85 of 317 field-years are too thin to form a curve.
ranked.why_this_rank: I re-fetched 2024 week 24 myself this session: HTTP 200, rowCount 46, len 46, sample row MIGLIANICO 2024-06-11 lat 42.3887 lon 14.3019 cv Montepulciano d'Abruzzo val {"media_catture":"2",...}. The skeptic re-ran the full 238-request sweep and reproduced the hunter's per-year counts EXACTLY (490/551/371/27/786/720/585), with all 3,530 id_survey values distinct and zero week-filter leakage. The model attack fails outright: schema 5 has exactly six fields, all of them things a technician reads off a trap or a bunch — no risk index, no degree-day, no DSS score. It ranks second because it is vine and numeric with real variance and point geometry, and loses first place only on the missing denominator, the near-total absence of treatment data, and the broken 2022/2024 panel seam. Data-quality caveat found by the skeptic and not the hunter: media_catture = '-2' exists (Ortona, 2020-06-16), a physically impossible negative catch proving the numeric field is served unvalidated.

ranked.name: ORCHARD/POLYPHAGOUS x HALYOMORPHA HALYS x EMILIA-ROMAGNA (Cimice.Net, UniBO BIG / Regione E-R)
ranked.region: Emilia-Romagna (MO, RA, FE, FC, BO, PC — confirmed from trap-name prefixes in the payload)
ranked.outcome_type: COUNT (per-trap, per-week integer captures split by life stage: Adulti, Giovani II-III, Giovani IV-V)
ranked.panel_stability: STABLE-BUT-SHRINKING, and the hunter cherry-picked. Traps per season 139/165/101/89/68/51/45 (2020-2026). Best adjacent overlaps are real (2023->2024 63/68 = 93%, 2024->2025 49/51 = 96%) but the hunter quoted only those two; the skeptic measured the weakest transition at 2022->2023 = 63/89 = 71% and 2020->2021 = 136/165 = 82%. Join across years on 'name', never on 'gid' (per-record id, changes annually). 2020 additionally carries two egg-mass fields no other season has, and a phantom EMPTY-STRING week key that crashes a naive sorted(keys, key=int) loader.
ranked.geographic_resolution: Point lat/lon (WGS84) per individual physical trap, with stable trap code (MO29, RA31) and 'installed' epoch
ranked.defence_data: NO. None at all. You cannot distinguish genuinely low pressure from a sprayed block — the single most limiting property for any efficacy or advisory use.
ranked.adama_relevance: H. halys reshaped insecticide demand in Emilia-Romagna fruit growing and is a listed secondary vine pest. But there is NO crop attribution in the served data: the skeptic probed for a richer per-trap endpoint (getTrapsData.php, 404) and grepped the front-end and config for coltura/crop/pero/pesco/frutteto with zero hits. You cannot condition a crop-specific model on it. Also NO licence statement anywhere on the host, so redistribution terms are UNKNOWN — a real commercial/legal risk, though not a data defect.
ranked.backtest_potential: The largest verified per-site numeric Italian series in the vine/orchard space (17,742 non-null trap-week records over 7 seasons, nonzero-catch rate 70-79%), free, no auth, point coordinates, weekly. Enough N to compute a genuinely meaningful skill metric for a population/phenology component — which is more than most candidates here can support. Two corrections that matter operationally: the hunter's claim that the co-hosted weather grid shares the SAME weekly keys is FALSE (skeptic decoded prec_day for msId=14 and found EXACT key intersection = ZERO; trap keys are Italian wall-clock, weather keys are UTC midnight, offset varies 3600/7200s with DST). The join is still feasible after DST-aware date normalisation, but it must be built, not assumed. Observation count is ~9% lower than claimed: 1,690 of 19,432 rows are all-null placeholders. 2026 is an incomplete open season.
ranked.why_this_rank: The skeptic's hardest attack was that 'getHeatmapTrapsData' implied server-side kriging, which would have made it MODELLED output. It failed decisively: every one of ~6,300 life-stage values scanned in msId=14 is a pure integer string with zero decimal points, the distribution is heavily zero-inflated (3,109 zeros, 430 ones, 314 twos, tail to 320), values sit at fixed coordinates carrying physical trap codes, and the contrast with the SAME host's weather layer — continuous floats like 38.0000057220459 on ~0.063x0.045 deg polygons — proves only the weather product is interpolated. This is ground truth. It ranks third on raw data power and geometry alone, and no higher, because it delivers population pressure with no crop, no damage measure, no incidence, no severity and no defence data — it can backtest a phenology/population component of a disease-intelligence tool and nothing more.

ranked.name: VITE x PERONOSPORA (Plasmopara viticola) x ABRUZZO (AgroAmbiente Abruzzo, crop=3, survey_schema=7)
ranked.region: Abruzzo (Chieti 2,265 rows, Pescara 591, Teramo 528, L'Aquila 110; 60 comuni)
ranked.outcome_type: PRESENCE — skeptic CORRECTED the hunter's 'SEVERITY'. Leaf variable is an ordinal presence class (49 nessuna / 51 bassa / 50 media / 52 alta). Only the bunch variable carries percentage bands (53 nessuna, 55 1-5%, 54 5-10%, 56 >15%), and that is INCIDENCE, not severity.
ranked.panel_stability: NO PANEL. 285 field-years across 2021-2026 (61/41/7/48/54/74 distinct id_field per year) and ZERO id_field present in all six years. Only 63 of 285 field-years contain even one positive observation. A fixed-site time series cannot be built.
ranked.geographic_resolution: Point lat/lon per vineyard field + comune, monitoring area, province
ranked.defence_data: STRUCTURALLY YES, PRACTICALLY NO. 'data ultimo tratt.', 'prodotto' and 'prodotto in miscela' exist on the record (actives include fluopicolide, folpet, ametoctradina, mandipropamide, cimoxanil, benalaxil-M) and a difesa regime flag (biologico/integrato/integrato volontario) is served — a mirror of the incumbent's structure. But the skeptic found only 182 of 3,494 rows (5.2%) carry a treatment date, and only TWELVE rows in six years carry BOTH a treatment date AND a non-zero disease reading. The hunter's headline 'dated georeferenced outcome + what was sprayed' is overstated by roughly an order of magnitude.
ranked.adama_relevance: HIGHEST pathosystem fit of anything ranked here — it is literally the incumbent's disease, on the incumbent's crop, in a second Italian region, on a sibling of the incumbent's own API. If the product is a vine downy-mildew engine, this is the only surviving out-of-Toscana Italian series that speaks the same language.
ranked.backtest_potential: LOW as a primary target, GENUINE as a corroborating layer. The killer is positive-event famine: corrected six-year tallies are foglie nessuna 3,313 / bassa 81 / media 32 / alta 2, grappoli nessuna 3,245 / 1-5% 32 / 5-10% 5 / >15% 5 — only 126 rows (3.6%) are non-zero on either organ, and only TWO 'alta' leaf readings exist in six years. Worse, the signal year is the empty year: 2023, the catastrophic central-Italy peronospora season, returned 16 rows from 7 fields, and both 'alta' readings fall in it. Any AUC/accuracy computed against the full 3,494 would be dominated by the base rate of zeros and would be meaningless. Usable only for presence-only positive events (the 126 rows, or the 63 positive field-years). Voluntary participation also means a missing record is NOT a zero, so negatives are untrustworthy.
ranked.why_this_rank: Fourth, not higher, purely on statistical power. The source itself is sound and the model attack fails cleanly: schema 7 is a human data-entry select-widget form with uid, id_field, note and guid_rilievo, and the leaked SQL joins survey to field/farm_center/user — no risk index, no degree-day, no 'condizioni favorevoli'. Skeptic-found defects the hunter missed and which any harvester must handle: the same field is stored sometimes as JSON integer 49 and sometimes as string "49" (a naive tally silently splits every class in two); user_access=validated and =test return identical counts so test rows cannot be excluded; the leaked SQL excludes orgs flagged visible='private' so the public feed is a subset of unknown size; omitting &week silently returns only the latest week; and a bogus parameter returns ok:true with NO rowCount key at all (reproduced with difesa=xyz). Rank it as auxiliary evidence that a vine downy-mildew event happened at a place and date, never as a scoring denominator.

ranked.name: VITE x PERONOSPORA x ITALIA — untreated-control (testimone) trials in the Giornate Fitopatologiche Atti (AIPP / Universita di Bologna)
ranked.region: Multi-region Italy: verified sites in Piemonte (AT, CN), Abruzzo (PE), Veneto (VR), Emilia-Romagna (RA)
ranked.outcome_type: SEVERITY and INCIDENCE as TWO SEPARATE PAIRED COLUMNS — the hunter conflated them. Papers label them explicitly: 'Severita%' (intensita = % leaf surface or % berries affected) and 'Incidenza%' (diffusione = % leaves or bunches with symptoms). Never average them. In some papers severity is a Townsend-Heuberger INDEX computed from an ordinal 0-7 class scale, so severity scales are not comparable across papers.
ranked.panel_stability: NONE. This is a corpus of scattered site-seasons, not a series. Trials are re-sited every season by whichever CRO or institute runs them. The best continuity found was within a single paper (same Pianella PE vineyard in 2016 and 2017), never as a designed panel.
ranked.geographic_resolution: MIXED and worse than the hunter claimed. Some papers name the comune ('agro di Pianella (PE)'); the contract CROs (Agrea, Sagea, Agri2000) give only 'in provincia di Verona / Cuneo / Ravenna'. Province-level siting is too coarse for an honest Plasmopara weather join, where 20 km of rainfall difference changes the answer. Partial mitigation: some papers publish their own per-trial rainfall (mm and events >5mm).
ranked.defence_data: BEST IN THE ENTIRE SET, and this is its real and unique strength. Every untreated control is paired with fully documented treated theses — product, active substance, dose, application dates — with ANOVA and Duncan/SNK letter separation and Abbott efficacy computed against the control.
ranked.adama_relevance: Exactly the incumbent pathosystem, and ADAMA and its competitors contribute trials to this corpus themselves, so the format is already familiar to the Italian team. Its highest-value use is as a DEFENCE-EFFECT reference (treated vs untreated with full product/dose/date), which is directly commercially relevant.
ranked.backtest_potential: MODERATE and structurally constrained — and I rank it here despite the skeptic having strengthened it substantially. He retrieved SIX seasons (2013, 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021) and 50 untreated-control values versus the hunter's one, and demolished the hunter's stated fatal weakness: the giornatefitopatologiche.it 403 is a www-vs-apex artifact, the apex serves HTTP 200, the real index is /it/elenco/24 listing 33 editions 1962-2024, and full-text PDFs download free at /it/download/23?idMat=NNNNNN with no login. The disqualifying limits are epidemiological, not access: (1) trials are DELIBERATELY sited under high pressure (one paper says outright its vineyard is 'molto soggetto ad infezioni peronosporiche'), so controls systematically overstate ambient pressure; (2) the controls SATURATE — verified readings of 100 / 98,9 / 100 / 99,4 / 100 / 100 / 100 / 100,0 — and a control pinned at 100% carries zero discriminative information; (3) there are no true negatives, so it can confirm a season WAS conducive but never that one was quiet.
ranked.why_this_rank: Fifth because it is the only Italian source of UNCONFOUNDED Plasmopara epidemic intensity with matched treatment records — genuinely unique — but it cannot score a risk model. Two traps for any harvester, both established by the skeptic: the entire 2008 edition returns HTTP 200 + content-type application/pdf + ZERO BYTES (12 of 12 sampled), a textbook '200 is not data' failure that would silently record 2008 as 'no trials' — mark it ACCESS_FAILED, never zero; and the archive PDFs embed subsetted CFF fonts with no ToUnicode CMap, so text extraction returns ciphertext. The 2018 files are a uniform +29 shift (decodable), but the 2022 files use an arbitrary per-file substitution in which the DIGITS are remapped with no linguistic redundancy to crack them — a cipher-solving harvester would emit silently WRONG numbers. Budget OCR, not parsing. Keyword harvesting on 'peronospora' will also pull in MODELLED_RISK papers (2008 id 3892 model validation; 2014 id 4370 vite.net DSS), so per-paper triage is mandatory.

ranked.name: FRUMENTO x OIDIO-SEPTORIA-FUSARIOSI-RUGGINI x TOSCANA (AgroAmbiente.info, crop=19, survey_schemas 74 and 75)
ranked.region: Toscana (principally Arezzo / Valdichiana; e.g. Marciano della Chiana)
ranked.outcome_type: SEVERITY — paired frequenza and intensita ordinal classes, %-anchored and rank-ordered via the survey_code 'order_n' field (0/5/10/25/50/75), so each class decodes to a numeric severity anchor. frequenza(oidio) = Nessuna / Bassa <10% / Media 10-25% / Alta >25%; intensita = Nessuna / 5-lieve / 10-media / 25-grave / 50-gravissima / 75-completa.
ranked.panel_stability: ROTATING AND THIN. id_field overlap at week 20: 2020(50)->2021(38) share 33; 2021->2022(45) share 20; 2022->2023(44) share 36; 2023->2024(48) share 27; 2024->2025(44) share 42; 2025->2026(50) share 30. Only 10 id_field values appear in all 7 verified years. Same coordinates recur on the same date, i.e. multiple plots or cultivars per site.
ranked.geographic_resolution: Point lat/lon per plot + ISTAT comune code, comune name, sub-area, province
ranked.defence_data: UNKNOWN — stated honestly by the hunter and NOT resolved. The four wheat schemas are phenology plus three disease schemas; no treatments schema was found and schema 76 'Altre avversita' was not checked for treatment fields. Do not assume either way.
ranked.adama_relevance: Cereal fungicides are a core ADAMA Italy category, and Septoria and the rusts are strongly weather-driven, so this exercises the SAME class of infection logic a downy-mildew engine encodes, on a different pathosystem. Cheap generalisation check rather than a primary benchmark.
ranked.backtest_potential: LOW-MODERATE. Only ~44-50 plots per week and 10 id_field values common to all 7 verified years, so per-site power is poor. The classes are ordinal bands with no sample denominator ('10-25%' is a band, not a number), unlike the olive series. It is a COMPOUND schema — one row carries three diseases at once — so a per-disease series must be unpicked and a 'Nessuna' class is indistinguishable from 'not assessed'. Only week 20 was audited; other weeks unverified. Same 2006-2019 server SQL block caps history at 2020-2026.
ranked.why_this_rank: Sixth, and flagged with an explicit epistemic caveat: NO SKEPTIC REVIEWED THIS CANDIDATE. Everything above it (except where noted) survived an adversarial pass; this one did not receive one. The hunter's verification discipline on the sibling crop=2 and crop=3 endpoints was independently confirmed sound by a skeptic, and he did retrieve the decode table (filter.survey_code, 110 code definitions) that proves the classes are %-anchored and ordered — without which the 'val' payload is meaningless integer ids. I rank it here because it is the cheapest possible pathosystem-generalisation test on an API already being harvested for the incumbent, not because its power is adequate. Treat n_observations=550 as hunter-claimed, not skeptic-confirmed.

ranked.name: VITE x FLAVESCENZA DORATA (+ vettore S. titanus) x PIEMONTE (Settore Fitosanitario A1703B, Progetti Pilota)
ranked.region: Piemonte (7 Progetto Pilota areas with published incidence: Alessandrino, Canavese & Eporediese, Barolo & Barbaresco, Doglianese & Monregalese, Gaviese, Nicese & Val Tiglione, Area Moscato Cuneese; Valle Susa publishes vector catches only)
ranked.outcome_type: INCIDENCE ('incidenza media FD in vigneto' = mean % symptomatic vines), plus a COUNT vector layer (mean S. titanus per trap) and a third administrative layer of 'segnalazioni' which is a count of reports of neglected plots and must NOT be used as disease ground truth despite the word 'rischio' appearing beside it.
ranked.panel_stability: NOT A FIXED PANEL, with explicit filtering. Roster grows 450 (2022) -> 532 (2023) -> 608 (2024) -> 616 (2025), and both official documents repeat the caveat 'Dati elaborati escludendo i valori anomali e i vigneti con meno di 7 trappole consegnate'. No per-vineyard IDs published, so within-area stability is unverifiable from outside.
ranked.geographic_resolution: Progetto Pilota AREA — a cluster of 9 to 92 comuni. Alessandrino collapses 92 comuni into one annual mean. Underlying data is per-appezzamento but is not published.
ranked.defence_data: NO — and worse, the outcome is POLICY-CONFOUNDED. Symptomatic vines are under mandatory legal removal (estirpo) and insecticide dates are fixed by decree per area. The companion strategy PDF tabulates enforcement actions (ESTIRPO SINGOLE PIANTE 44, VIGNETO TIPO 2 42, VITI IN INCOLTI TIPO 3 71, IN BOSCAGLIE TIPO 4 93, COMPLETAMENTO 9). The near-monotonic 2022->2025 decline partly measures ENFORCEMENT INTENSITY, not epidemiology.
ranked.adama_relevance: FD is the single largest mandatory-treatment driver in Italian viticulture and the reason for the lotta obbligatoria insecticide regime against S. titanus, covering Barolo/Barbaresco, Moscato, Gavi, Nizza and Alessandrino. Commercially first-rank; scientifically the wrong shape for a weather-driven engine.
ranked.backtest_potential: LOW. Total publicly numeric content is ~42 values across 7 areas x 4 years. The only high-resolution signal — the fortnightly S. titanus flight curves — is CHART-ONLY: the skeptic confirmed by extraction that pages 4/9/25/33/41/49/57/64 yield the date axis labels and ticks 0/5/10/15 and ZERO plotted series values. No CSV, no API, no per-vineyard microdata. Archival fragility is real: all four probes for the 2023/2024 editions returned HTTP 404 (each a 154,798-byte branded HTML error page — the '200-is-not-data' trap in reverse), so 2022-2024 figures survive only as back-reported slide text.
ranked.why_this_rank: Seventh: unimpeachable as an observation, nearly unusable as a scoring target. The skeptic fetched the underlying protocol 'Metodo monitoraggio scafoideo' (HTTP 200, 135,651 bytes) and confirmed PHYSICAL COUNTING — 'conteggiare le forme giovanili (neanidi e ninfe) su 5 foglie per pianta in prossimita del ceppo', two samplings per vineyard, sequential-sampling stop thresholds, recorded on a paper scheda. No model anywhere. He also found FOUR regional incidence values the hunter missed (2022 7,01% / 2023 7,76% / 2024 5,22% / 2025 4,87%) and three defects the hunter did not catch: the two official documents published the same month DISAGREE on the 2025 regional S. titanus figure (2,2 vs 2,1), proving these are hand-transcribed slide numbers not a data export; the hunter double-counted 'Valle Belbo' and 'Area Moscato Cuneese' as separate areas; and Valle Susa has no incidence series at all. Keep as a high-credibility direction-of-travel corroborator. The genuinely valuable asset — 616 plots x 4 years x ~10,400 traps — exists behind the PDF and is SOURCE_NOT_PUBLIC.

ranked.name: VITE x SCAPHOIDEUS TITANUS (adulti, rete trappole cromotropiche) x VENETO (U.O. Fitosanitario)
ranked.outcome_type: PERCENTAGE (share of monitored vineyards below a trap-catch threshold of <2 individuals on 3 traps, split bio vs conventional). The underlying site-level datum is an ordinal BINNED COUNT (adults per 3 traps per fortnight) in six classes: 0, <2, 3-9, 10-29, 30-99, >100.
ranked.panel_stability: DESIGNED-STABLE BUT UNAUDITABLE, with documented drift. The same 'Rete di monitoraggio regionale' is re-read annually, but the vineyard list is never published so panel identity cannot be verified from outside. Denominators wobble WITHIN single documents (2026 prose says 156 vigneti / 468 trappole while its own map legend says 157; 2025 prose says 159 while the reprinted map says 157). Stratum label drifted from 'difesa integrata' (2024) to 'difesa convenzionale' (2025-26) with no declaration.
ranked.geographic_resolution: PUBLISHED AS BOTH: a regional aggregate stratified by defence regime, AND — the hunter materially understated this — a GEOREFERENCED POINT MAP, one symbol per monitored vineyard over a Veneto basemap with province labels, binned into six catch classes with per-class counts printed in the legend, and the prior year's map reprinted beneath. That is ~157 site-level ordinal observations per mapped turno (157 for 2026 + 157 for 2025 = 314 site classifications), recoverable to a few km by digitising the points.
ranked.defence_data: YES, and it is a rare free efficacy signal: every reading is split bio vs conventional/integrata, against a legally mandated treatment calendar. 2026 turno 1: 42% bio vs 78% conventional below threshold.
ranked.adama_relevance: S. titanus control is a compulsory, monitoring-informed insecticide programme across the entire Veneto vineyard in the Glera/Prosecco belt — this network directly governs spray timing and application count, which is precisely the commercial decision a vector-control recommendation targets.
ranked.backtest_potential: LOW-MODERATE and bottlenecked by extraction, not by validity. Only ~2 observation events are published per season, NOT fortnightly through September as the hunter claimed — the skeptic fetched bulletins 17, 19 and 20 of 2026 and found n.17 merely announces the upcoming trap replacement while n.19 and n.20 contain NO regional monitoring section at all. Everything requires PDF text extraction plus raster point digitisation; there is no CSV or API. 2022 and 2023 are HTTP 404 on the live site and web.archive.org was ACCESS_FAILED through this proxy, so 2023 is probably recoverable elsewhere but was not recovered.
ranked.why_this_rank: Eighth, and it earns its place on an unusual piece of evidence: the skeptic independently VALIDATED THE PUBLISHED ARITHMETIC. For 2026 he read the map legend classes and reconstructed bio 26 = 8+3+3+5+3+4 with (8+3)/26 = 42.3% matching the stated 42%; conv 131 = 78+25+15+5+4+4 with (78+25)/131 = 78.6% matching the stated 78%; and unacceptable-density classes 12+13 = 25/157 = 15.9% matching the stated 16%. Three independent checks pass, which is strong evidence the aggregates are honest reductions of real site data. ONE THING DOES NOT RECONCILE and anyone using this must know it: the 2025 bulletin prose says 68% for the conventional stratum, but the same 2025 turno-1 map reprinted in the 2026 bulletin gives 0[68] + <2[32] of [131] = 76.3% — off by 8 points, with the suspicious coincidence that 68 is exactly the class-0 count. Either the 2025 prose was wrong or the series was silently re-cut. Backtest against the MAP class counts, never the prose percentages. The model attack fails completely: these are physical yellow sticky traps (mod. Glutor 40x25 cm), 3 per vineyard, swapped and counted by technicians on a fixed turno — circularity NONE.

ranked.name: VITE x PERONOSPORA (rilievi settimanali di zona DOC) x FRIULI-VENEZIA GIULIA (ERSA, bollettini dei Consorzi DOC)
ranked.region: Friuli-Venezia Giulia (6 DOC zones: Carso, Collio, Colli Orientali, Isonzo, Grave, Aquileia-Latisana-Annia)
ranked.outcome_type: PRESENCE — a dated presence/absence-of-new-infection statement per zone-week, in free prose. Confirmed correct as labelled; occasional percentages appear (2017 '30% dei vigneti trattati', 2021 '>50% delle osservazioni') but with inconsistent denominators and inconsistent spatial scope, so they cannot be promoted to a clean INCIDENCE series.
ranked.panel_stability: STABLE AT ZONE LEVEL, UNKNOWABLE BELOW IT. The same 6 DOC zones are covered weekly from April/May to August every season. But 'vigneti monitorati' / 'siti monitorati' are NEVER enumerated in any of the nine PDFs the skeptic read — no denominator, no vineyard identifiers. Only the tignole trap stations are named and recurrent (Sagrado GO, Prepotto TS).
ranked.geographic_resolution: DOC zone (a named cluster of comuni). Named locality only for the Carso tignole trap stations.
ranked.defence_data: YES in an unusual form: the same archives publish, with the same numbering and the same date, separate AVVISI DI TRATTAMENTO for Produzione INTEGRATA and Produzione BIOLOGICA — a trace of the RECOMMENDED defence aligned to the observed outcome. That is rare. It is recommendation, not application record.
ranked.adama_relevance: The incumbent pathosystem in a first-rank Nordest wine region with intense anti-downy-mildew defence, weekly, over 11+ seasons. ERSA also cites the ARPA-OSMER weather stations by name (Sagrado, Duino Prepotto, Sgonico, San Dorligo, Bicinicco, Codroipo, Fagagna, Brugnera, S. Vito), making a zone-level weather join realistic.
ranked.backtest_potential: WEAK BUT LEGITIMATE, and it is an NLP project, not a data pull. Roughly 6 zones x 15-20 weeks x 11+ seasons of binary presence-of-new-infection, plus a genuinely numeric COUNT sub-series for tignole at named stations in recent years. Usable ONLY for scoring whether a tool flagged risk in the weeks a technician actually recorded new infections; NOT usable for severity or incidence calibration. Corpus size is large (~3,500-3,700 public PDFs across 6 consortium archives, no auth).
ranked.why_this_rank: Ninth because the extraction hazards are severe and specific, and every one was confirmed in-document by the skeptic. (1) CIRCULARITY IS REAL AND ADJACENT: Carso n.5/2024 prints 'I modelli previsionali danno possibili infezioni con medio rischio' three times, once directly beneath each of the peronospora, oidio and black rot OBSERVATION lines — same font, same section. Get the split wrong and you score a model against a model. (2) A NAIVE KEYWORD EXTRACTOR PRODUCES AN ACTIVELY WRONG SERIES: in Carso n.20/2020 the only paragraph headed 'Peronospora' sits under STRATEGIE DI DIFESA and is pure spray advice, while the real observation lives in an 'OSSERVAZIONI IN CAMPO' block that never names the pathogen. (3) SPATIAL MISATTRIBUTION: Carso n.12/2021 embeds a REGIONAL '>50% delle osservazioni' beside the zone observation. (4) FILENAME YEARS ARE CORRUPT: a file named ..._N_5_DEL_2024_ZONA_DOC_CARSO.pdf has a body reading 'N. 5 DEL 8 MAGGIO 2026' — key on the PDF body date or the upload prefix, never the filename. (5) 2016-2017 is materially weaker: the 2016 peronospora section is favourable-conditions language plus a regional pressure statement, not a Carso rilievo. Upside the hunter missed: the CCC archive floor is 2011, not 2015/2016 — the series is older than advertised. The underlying structured per-site database (difesafitosanitaria.ersa.fvg.it/.../rilievivite/) is behind a login: AUTH_REQUIRED.

ranked.name: OLIVO x XYLELLA FASTIDIOSA x PUGLIA (Osservatorio Fitosanitario regionale, open data CC-BY-4.0)
ranked.region: Puglia (106 comuni; Bari 336,971 samples, Brindisi 181,925, Taranto 146,868, BAT 15,004, Foggia 7,855)
ranked.outcome_type: PRESENCE — two independent per-sample fields: RISULTATO (laboratory diagnostic, Positivo 5,241 / Negativo 683,390) and SINTOMO (technician's field symptom call, Presente 21,250 / Assente 667,279).
ranked.panel_stability: ROTATING BY DESIGN and this is its central flaw. It is an adaptive quarantine delimitation survey whose sampling follows the demarcated-zone boundary as the infection front moves. Rows per year 176,505 / 233,753 / 187,264 / 91,109 (2020-2023); only 15 of 106 comuni sampled in all four years. The same trees are not resampled.
ranked.geographic_resolution: POINT — decimal lat/lon (WGS84) per individual sampled plant, plus COMUNE and PROVINCIA. The finest resolution of anything found in any lane.
ranked.adama_relevance: LOW and I will not inflate it. Crop is olive (597,277 of 688,631 samples) and there are ZERO Vitis records — checked explicitly. Xylella has no curative chemical control, so the only commercial link runs through the compulsory Philaenus spumarius vector-control programme, which this dataset does not record. Its honest value to ADAMA Italy is methodological.
ranked.backtest_potential: EXCELLENT AS A PIPELINE SANDBOX, POOR AS AN EPIDEMIOLOGICAL TARGET. 688,631 dated, georeferenced, lab-confirmed rows at 82 MB over plain HTTPS with no auth make it the right place to prove out geocoding, comune aggregation, panel handling, class imbalance and an observation-to-weather join before pointing the pipeline at a thin vine series. But 'Positivo' is a regulatory verdict on a RISK-TARGETED sample, so prevalence is a function of where inspectors were sent: the collapse from 2,869 positives (2021) to 242 (2022) to 124 (2023) coincides with a large change in sampling geography and must NOT be read as an incidence time series without area-normalisation. Positives are 0.76% of rows. The 2023 portion is undocumented in the catalogue description and may be a partial campaign; the newer CAMP_2020_2023.csv resource is registered with an EMPTY download URL, so the update path is unclear.
ranked.why_this_rank: Ranked LAST of the ten deliberately: data quality must not outrank relevance. This is by a wide margin the best-engineered Italian phytosanitary dataset in existence, and it is on the wrong crop with the wrong pathogen family for a weather-driven fungal-disease engine. It was independently downloaded and profiled by THREE separate hunters in three different lanes who each parsed the full 688,631 rows and reported identical distributions (year histogram, RISULTATO split, SINTOMO split, host-species counts) — the strongest cross-lane corroboration of any candidate here, though no skeptic ran a formal adversarial pass on it. File format gotchas: semicolon-delimited, latin-1 (fails a naive utf-8 read), comma decimal separator in coordinates, and the filename says 2020_2022 while the content runs into 2023.

ranking.reasoning:
HEADLINE: nothing found in five lanes beats the incumbent, and I am not going to pretend otherwise. The incumbent's specific combination — a dated per-visit vine downy-mildew outcome (ordinal leaf class + percentage bunch bands + sporulazione yes/no) PLUS the date of last treatment PLUS the active ingredient actually applied PLUS defence regime as a first-class filter, on one auth-free API — is not matched by any Italian candidate surfaced here. Several candidates beat it on ONE axis; none beats it on the combination, and none is a vine-peronospora series with better properties.

WHERE INDIVIDUAL CANDIDATES DO BEAT THE INCUMBENT, honestly stated: (a) MEASUREMENT CALIBRATION — the Toscana olive series (rank 1) has a true fixed denominator (n=100 destructively sampled fruit per visit), so its outcome is a calibratable rate rather than an ordinal band; that is strictly better ground truth, on the wrong crop and the wrong pest class. (b) RAW N AND GEOMETRY — Cimice.Net (rank 3) delivers 17,742 non-null per-trap, per-week integer counts with physical trap coordinates over 7 seasons, more real observations than any vine candidate, with no crop attribution and no defence data. (c) DEFENCE DETAIL — the Giornate Fitopatologiche untreated-control corpus (rank 5) pairs an unconfounded epidemic curve with product, active substance, dose and application dates under ANOVA, which is richer defence information than any surveillance series including the incumbent; it is a corpus of scattered site-seasons with no panel, deliberate high-pressure siting, ceiling saturation and no true negatives.

WHAT I DID THIS SESSION: I re-fetched the top two ranked series myself rather than trusting the dossiers. Toscana crop=2 survey_schema=1, year 2024, week 36: HTTP 200, envelope ok=true, data.ok=true, rowCount 294, len(data) 294, verbatim val {"tot":"100","u":"0",...,"totale":0.0,"dannosa":0.0,"attiva":0.0} — real rows with the n=100 denominator visible. Abruzzo crop=3 survey_schema=5, year 2024, week 24: HTTP 200, rowCount 46, len 46, sample MIGLIANICO 2024-06-11, lat 42.3887531999297, lon 14.3019480024077, cv Montepulciano d'Abruzzo, val {"media_catture":"2",...}. Both reproduce the skeptics' counts exactly. Everything else in this ranking rests on lane evidence, and I have marked which entries a skeptic actually adjudicated.

RANKING PHILOSOPHY. I weighted, in order: (1) is it a real dated repeated OBSERVATION rather than a model output — every ranked entry passed this test under adversarial attack, and I note the specific attack that failed in each 'why_this_rank'; (2) can you compute a meaningful skill number from it (variance, N, denominator, true negatives); (3) panel and geographic resolution; (4) presence of defence/management data, without which you cannot separate low pressure from a sprayed block; (5) ADAMA Italy commercial relevance; (6) integration cost. I deliberately ranked the single best-engineered dataset in the whole exercise (Xylella Puglia, 688,631 georeferenced lab-confirmed rows) LAST, because data quality must not outrank relevance — it is olive, it is a vector-borne bacterium with no fungicide market, and it contains zero Vitis records.

WHAT I DID NOT RANK, AND WHY. Two candidates were REFUTED by skeptics and are excluded entirely: (i) POPILLIA JAPONICA x LOMBARDIA — the skeptic pulled the companion trap-registry layer and found all 20 traps sited at '2.2 Public sites' (15) or '2.4 Wild plants' (5), Pubblico_P 'Pubblico - Altro' x19, with no crop field and Varieta blank on every row; the 'vite' framing is the hunter's agronomic inference, not a property of the data. Worse, the 'Data' field is blank on all 20 rows and Catture23/24/25 are three wide columns bolted onto a single 2023-05-17 installation record — three undated numbers per site, not three dated observations, which kills the weather join. Add VARIO attract-and-kill devices taking up to 138,331 beetles per trap-season (the instrument is itself the intervention) and a Cittiglio reading of 5,653/5,741/5,743 (+2 beetles in a year against a 2.6x regional surge) that looks carried-forward. (ii) VITE x PERONOSPORA x UMBRIA untreated plots and (iii) VITE x FLAVESCENZA x VENETO monitoraggio massivo — both refuted: the Umbria 'testimone' at Bettona exists with numeric scorings in exactly ONE year (grep for 'testimon', 'Bettona' and '300 mq' in the 2024/2025 deck returns ZERO), and the Veneto mass survey publishes only bands ('3-5%' -> '1-2%') with the 2021 Veneto section containing no percent sign anywhere — the '237 vigneti / 1,17%' the hunter credited to Veneto is in fact the Friuli-Venezia Giulia section of the same PDF.

Also considered and NOT ranked, in rough order of what I would chase next: Abruzzo OIDIO on vine (crop=3 schema 8) — 4,037 rows verified 2020-2026, 169 fields, 60 comuni, 408 treatment dates, identical structure to the ranked Abruzzo peronospora entry and available on the same terms; it is a near-duplicate rather than an independent asset, but it is a second vine FUNGAL disease and is already verified. Lazio BACTROCERA OLEAE (agroambientelazio.it, OP LATIUM / SFR Lazio) — real destructive sampling with a stated protocol ('20 olive a pianta su 10 piante ... un totale di 200 olive') reported as 'Attacco rilevato: X%', 3 values read from 3 PDFs across 2 years, ~200 news items back to Aug 2020; genuinely usable but only bracketed per-zone weekly values with no coordinates. Veneto S. TITANUS NEANIDI (neanidi/pianta, pre- and post- mandatory treatment, 2025: 0,12 -> 0,02 integrata and 0,39 -> 0,07 biologica) — the closest thing to a natural experiment anyone found, but verified in one year only and just 4-8 numbers per season. Liguria FD and Liguria POPILLIA WFS layers — open OGC WFS, CC-BY, true point geolocation, but 116 and 150 binary points across 2 years and 1 year respectively, with a completely rotating panel and (for FD) an unresolved ambiguity about whether a positive means the phytoplasma or the vector. Umbria vine bulletins — 41 zone-week trap values and 8 peronospora range-percentages, ALL inside a two-month window of 2024. PNI Puglia 2024 — 708 rows at NUTS2 resolution, only 8 of them touching vine; an institutional lead, not a series. Trentino FEM untreated controls — correct experimental design, ZERO numeric data retrieved, PUBLIC_CLAIMED_NOT_VERIFIED. CREA Bilancio Fitosanitario Viticolo — survived skeptic review upgraded to 3 verified editions and 32 numbers, but it is region-year narrative prose at 7-16 values per edition with metrics that change between editions, and the skeptic caught the hunter labelling '(oltre il 90% di germogli colpiti)' as peronospora when the sentence attributes it to the 7-8 April FROST; I left it out of the ten because rank 5 through 10 already carry that kind of coarse corroboration with better provenance.

THE BIGGEST FINDING IS A NEGATIVE, AND IT IS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. There is no publicly available Italian vine-peronospora quantitative outcome series that improves on the incumbent. The lanes proved this rather than assuming it: dati.emilia-romagna.it CKAN returns nothing phytosanitary; dati.lombardia.it Socrata returns 0 for fitosanitar/popillia/flavescenza/vite/peronospora while returning 111 for 'agricoltura' (the API works, the data is absent); Geoportale Piemonte CSW returns 0 for flavescenza; dati.veneto.it has no CKAN at all (Liferay 404); dati.trentino.it does not even list Fondazione Edmund Mach as an organisation; data.civis.bz.it returns 0 for pflanzenschutz and wein; and dati.gov.it nationally yields exactly two usable phytosanitary outcome datasets, BOTH of which are Regione Puglia's merely harvested into the national catalogue. The genuinely valuable Italian vine data — Emilia-Romagna's 1,619-vineyard Flavescenza campaign, Veneto's 3,065-parcel / 2.79-million-vine survey and its per-vineyard S. titanus rows elaborated by Universita di Padova, Piemonte's 616 plots and 10,496 traps, FEM's untreated-control network, the Alto Adige untreated-plot 'serie storica' — all exists, is collected by app, is georeferenced, and is SOURCE_NOT_PUBLIC. The highest-return next action is not more scraping; it is formal data requests to the Settori/Servizi Fitosanitari of Emilia-Romagna, Veneto, Piemonte and PAT/FEM, plus MASAF Servizio Fitosanitario Centrale for the Piano Nazionale di Indagine returns.

ONE CROSS-CUTTING WARNING FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THE HARVESTER. The '200 is not data' failure mode is not hypothetical and appeared in at least five distinct forms across these lanes: HTTP 200 with envelope ok:true but data.ok:false carrying a PostgreSQL SQLSTATE[42883] error (Toscana, all years 2006-2019); HTTP 200 with ok:true and NO rowCount key at all when a parameter is bogus (Abruzzo, reproduced with difesa=xyz); HTTP 200 with content-type application/pdf and ZERO BYTES (Giornate Fitopatologiche, entire 2008 edition, 12 of 12 sampled); HTTP 200 carrying {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Invalid URL"}} (ArcGIS Popillia_japonica_2024 and _2026); and HTTP 404 returning a 154,798-byte branded HTML page that any size-based success check would score as a hit (Regione Piemonte). Assert on row counts and body content, never on status codes, and record every failure as ACCESS_FAILED rather than zero.

SCOPE: Italy only. No Spanish or French source was searched, fetched, ranked or evaluated at any point in my synthesis. Andalucia's RAIF was never queried and is excluded as instructed; two lanes noted that RAIF XML files present in a shared scratchpad belong to other work and were not opened. The only non-Italian material that touched any lane was incidental German and Austrian viticulture pages surfaced by German-language queries aimed at Alto Adige, plus two French DRAAF documents on Scaphoideus — all discarded on sight and itemised below. Alto Adige / Suedtirol material is retained as Italian despite German-language sourcing.

blocked_routes.what_a_real_browser_would_get: The 'Ersa - Rilievi Vite' data-entry back-end behind the FVG DOC bulletins. Served HTTP 200 (13,734 bytes) but the page is a username/password form. A credentialed browser would reach the structured per-site rilievi database that underlies the ~3,500-3,700 public bulletin PDFs — i.e. the coded per-vineyard peronospora observations rather than the technician's prose. Not attempted.

The Wayback availability API confirmed a Dec-2023 snapshot exists and is status 200, but fetching it returned HTTP 403 (24-byte body) and then 'curl (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' through the agent proxy. A normal browser on an unproxied network would very likely recover the 2022 and 2023 Veneto vine bulletin seasons, which are HTTP 404 on the live regional site. This is ACCESS_FAILED, never 'the 2023 season does not exist'. Same block hit the archived 2025 Lombardia Popillia weekly-catch page.

Suedtiroler Beratungsring fuer Obst- und Weinbau — operator of the Alto Adige UNTREATED CONTROL plots whose speakers explicitly reference a long 'serie storica' of untreated-plot bunch damage. Both the index and a known PDF failed at the OpenSSL layer with 'error 0A00018A: dh key too small'; the server negotiates a Diffie-Hellman key below the client's minimum. A browser with a permissive TLS profile would load it. This is the most likely home of a genuine long Italian peronospora untreated-plot series and it remains UNVERIFIED, not absent. Not circumvented.

The national Servizio Fitosanitario portal — the single most likely home for national surveillance numbers. WebFetch returned HTTP 503 twice; curl failed TLS chain verification three times (curl error 60) even with --cacert /root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt and CURL_CA_BUNDLE set. The page body was never seen. It is UNASSESSED, not empty.

AVEPA is the Veneto paying agency and a plausible holder of the parcel-level Flavescenza dorata records behind the 3,065-particella / 2.79-million-vine survey. Two curl attempts returned exit 35 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' (proxy reported ws_closed_mid_exchange); WebFetch returned HTTP 503 with no body. Nothing was obtained. ACCESS_FAILED, not zero.

Default-UA curl gets a 919-byte CloudFront 'Request blocked' page. IMPORTANT: this block was SOLVED without circumvention — it is a www-vs-apex artifact. The apex https://giornatefitopatologiche.it/ serves HTTP 200 with no blocking, the real index is /it/elenco/24 (33 editions 1962-2024 with per-edition paper counts), and free full-text PDFs download at /it/download/23?idMat=NNNNNN with no login. Listed here because the www host does block automated agents and the hunter's dossier wrongly recorded the archive as unreachable. Related and NOT solved: https://aipp.it/?s=bilancio+fitosanitario+vite returns HTTP 403 with a 0-byte body, so the AIPP regional deck archive could not be enumerated.

Campania SFR runs a real UTM-based (Unita territoriali di monitoraggio) weekly network, 1 March - 30 September, per province (AV, BN, CE, NA, SA), stating that bulletins report 'lo stato fitosanitario delle diverse colture rilevati nelle aziende di riferimento'. The index pages return HTTP 200 (10,903 and 27,905 bytes) but the PDF links are injected dynamically by JavaScript and ZERO pdf hrefs were extractable; not a single bulletin was opened. A JS-executing browser would list them. This is the most promising completely unchecked lead left in the centro-sud lane.

HTTP 500 with an empty (0-byte) body for every parameter combination tried, including with Referer, Origin and X-Requested-With headers. This is the aggregated time-series endpoint for the Cimice.Net network; the per-trap GeoJSON route works perfectly and is what was actually harvested, so this is ACCESS_FAILED on one route, not an absence of data. Separately, the site's own advertised bulk-download page https://big.csr.unibo.it/downloads/stink-bug/ returns HTTP 404 — there is no official bulk export.

blocked_routes.url: https://agricoltura.regione.emilia-romagna.it — Settore Fitosanitario, Flavescenza dorata per-vineyard monitoring records (2023-2024)
blocked_routes.what_a_real_browser_would_get: The campaign is real and large: 1,619 vineyards visited across 2023-2024 out of 1,800 selected (10% of ~18,000 regional vineyards), with visual inspection plus chromotropic traps for Scaphoideus titanus in ~120 vineyards. The published pages give only prose ('a possible change in trend', 'no Flavescenza detected in Rimini in 2024'). No per-vineyard incidence figures, no trap counts, no downloadable file exist anywhere public. This would be the single best vine candidate in Emilia-Romagna if released; today it requires a formal data request to the Settore Fitosanitario.

blocked_routes.url: https://www.regione.veneto.it — U.O. Fitosanitario, per-vineyard Scaphoideus titanus rows and the Flavescenza dorata parcel database elaborated by Universita di Padova
blocked_routes.what_a_real_browser_would_get: 156-159 vineyards x 3 traps, collected with a georeferenced regional app, plus the 3,065-particella / 2,792,208-plant repeat survey. What is published is the regional aggregate plus a raster point map. dati.veneto.it has no CKAN API at all (HTTP 404, Liferay error page) and dati.gov.it returns success:true with count:0 for 'flavescenza'. The Regione's own press release confirms the raw data goes to Universita di Padova to build RISK MODELS — so any richer series that eventually surfaces carries a real MODELLED_RISK contamination risk and must be requested as raw observations, not as elaborated output.

blocked_routes.url: https://www.regione.piemonte.it — Settore Fitosanitario A1703B, per-vineyard Progetti Pilota microdata (616 vineyards, ~10,496 traps, 2022-2025)
blocked_routes.what_a_real_browser_would_get: The aggregate PDF proves the microdata exists and documents the protocol — both the 'Scheda registrazione adulti scafoideo' (.xls recording template) and 'Metodo monitoraggio scafoideo' (.pdf, physical counting on 5 leaves per plant) are published. Only ~42 area-level annual numbers are public; the fortnightly S. titanus flight curves are chart-only raster with no extractable series values. Four probes for the 2023/2024 editions returned HTTP 404. Vineyard-level FD incidence plus fortnightly vector counts over 2022-2025 would be a first-class backtest ground truth and is available only by request.

blocked_routes.url: https://ctt.fmach.it — Fondazione Edmund Mach, per-site numeric readings from the untreated-control (testimoni non trattati) vine network, Trentino
blocked_routes.what_a_real_browser_would_get: FEM runs untreated control parcels alongside treated vineyards and reads them weekly with a georeferenced smartphone app, with ~100 co-located weather stations at meteo.fmach.it and 4,797 ha monitored in 2021 (47% of provincial vineyard area). The public bulletins carry ONLY qualitative judgements ('la diffusione di peronospora e oidio e in genere molto bassa'). dati.trentino.it does not list Fondazione Edmund Mach as an organisation at all and returns count 0 for fitosanitario/peronospora/vite/trappole/flavescenza; the bulletin page exposes only the 2026 season. ZERO numeric rows retrieved — marked PUBLIC_CLAIMED_NOT_VERIFIED. This is the correct experimental design for the incumbent pathosystem and is the best target for a formal request to FEM / Servizio Fitosanitario PAT.

lanes.lane_notes:
COSA HO EFFETTIVAMENTE SCARICATO E LETTO (non solo HTTP 200): 8 PDF di bollettino ERSA/consorzi FVG, 4 PDF di bollettino viticolo Veneto (2 del 2025 e 2 del 2026) piu 1 copia Coldiretti Verona, 1 PDF di bollettino FEM Trentino, e 8 pagine di archivio ERSA paginate. Tutte le cifre riportate nei candidati sono state lette dal corpo del documento, mai dedotte.

VENETO - il risultato principale della lane. Oltre alle 'annate agrarie' ARPAV gia scartate come prosa, il Veneto ha una vera rete quantitativa: la Rete regionale di monitoraggio di Scaphoideus titanus della U.O. Fitosanitario, 155-159 vigneti con 3 trappole cromotropiche ciascuno (468-477 trappole), letta ogni due settimane da inizio luglio a fine settembre, piu due rilievi stagionali sulle forme giovanili espressi in neanidi/pianta. Ho verificato numeri reali per il 2025 e per il 2026, con i valori 2024 citati dentro il bollettino 2025 e coerenti con quelli letti nel 2026 (35%/68% nel 2025 ricompaiono come 'lo scorso anno' nel bollettino 2026): la catena e internamente consistente. IL LIMITE STRUTTURALE: cio che e pubblico e solo l'aggregato regionale per regime di difesa. Le righe per vigneto esistono, sono georeferenziate (raccolte con app regionale) e vengono elaborate dall'Universita di Padova nell'ambito di un database regionale unico sulla flavescenza dorata, ma non sono pubblicate. Questa e la richiesta dati piu remunerativa che questa lane produce.

VENETO - cosa NON e utilizzabile. Il bollettino viticolo regionale su peronospora e oidio e prosa pura ('non sono stati notati sviluppi infettivi di rilievo'), esattamente come le annate agrarie: DESCRIPTION_ONLY, confermato leggendo i bollettini n.20/2025 e n.12/2026 per intero. La tabella fenologica di Scaphoideus per stazione di monitoraggio esiste ma e inserita come IMMAGINE nel PDF (pagina con 6 immagini e nessun testo tabellare), quindi richiederebbe OCR; non l'ho estratta e non ne riporto contenuti. Il portale dati.veneto.it non espone API CKAN (HTTP 404 su /api/3/action/package_search): nessun open data fitosanitario regionale.

FRIULI-VENEZIA GIULIA - il corpus piu grande. Gli archivi ERSA dei bollettini dei Consorzi DOC sono pubblici, paginati e scaricabili senza autenticazione: Carso 13 pagine, Grave 21, Colli Orientali 22, Collio 18, Isonzo 23, Aquileia-Latisana-Annia 21, Collio-Carso pre-2016 4 pagine, a 30 voci per pagina, cioe dell'ordine di 3.500-3.700 documenti dal 2015/2016 al 2026. Contengono rilievi settimanali di campo su peronospora, oidio e black rot per zona DOC e, in modo intermittente, tabelle numeriche di catture di Lobesia botrana ed Eupoecilia ambiguella per stazione nominata (Sagrado GO, Prepotto TS nel Carso). Contengono anche, con la stessa numerazione e la stessa data, gli AVVISI DI TRATTAMENTO separati per Produzione Integrata e Produzione Biologica: e una traccia della difesa raccomandata allineata all'esito osservato, cosa rara. IL LIMITE: l'esito peronosporico e prosa, non una classe ordinale codificata, e il fraseggio cambia fra zone e annate; il formato delle catture cambia (tabella nel 2024/2026, prosa nel 2020/2023); e il database sorgente 'Ersa - Rilievi Vite' (difesafitosanitaria.ersa.fvg.it/rilievivite/) e dietro login, quindi i rilievi strutturati per sito sono AUTH_REQUIRED. Attenzione al rischio di circolarita: gli stessi PDF riportano accanto all'osservazione l'output dei modelli Goidanich e RIMpro; un estrattore ingenuo mescolerebbe osservazione e modello.

TRENTINO - il disegno giusto, i numeri assenti. FEM gestisce una rete di testimoni NON TRATTATI accanto ai vigneti trattati e li legge ogni settimana, ma nel bollettino pubblico il risultato e solo qualitativo. Ho verificato che il portale open data provinciale (dati.trentino.it) non contiene nulla di fitosanitario e che Fondazione Edmund Mach non compare nemmeno nell'elenco delle organizzazioni del portale. Il sito fitoemergenze.fmach.it e solo divulgativo. La pagina dei bollettini FEM espone solo la stagione 2026, quindi non ho potuto verificare la profondita d'archivio. Da trattare come bersaglio di richiesta dati, non come fonte pronta.

ALTO ADIGE - LANE VUOTA, e lo dico come risultato, non come assenza di ricerca. Il catalogo open data provinciale data.civis.bz.it risponde count 0 per 'pflanzenschutz' e per 'wein' (HTTP 200 con zero risultati, verificato: e proprio zero righe, non un errore di parametro); sotto 'landwirtschaft' ci sono 6 dataset, tutti amministrativi o zootecnici. Il sito del Suedtiroler Beratungsring (www.beratungsring.org) NON e raggiungibile da questo ambiente: fallimento TLS 'dh key too small' a livello OpenSSL, quindi ACCESS_FAILED e non 'nessun dato'; il sottodominio www3.beratungsring.org risponde ma non espone dati di monitoraggio. Di Laimburg ho visto solo riferimenti a prove sperimentali (pressione peronosporica a Piglon 2012-2014, prove su Rulaender) che sarebbero comunque monosito e sperimentali, non sorveglianza: non le ho verificate e non le riporto come candidato. Se questa lane va ripresa, l'Alto Adige va riattaccato con un client TLS meno restrittivo e con l'Agrar- und Forstbericht provinciale.

SCOPE: nessuna ricerca condotta su Spagna o Francia. Le fonti tedesche e austriache emerse incidentalmente dalle query in lingua tedesca sono elencate in non_italian_discarded e scartate."

candidates.issue: Halyomorpha halys (cimice asiatica / brown marmorated stink bug)
candidates.crop: Polyphagous — pheromone traps sited in fruit orchards (pear, peach) and field margins; crop of each trap site is NOT recorded in the served data
candidates.region: Emilia-Romagna (provinces MO, RA, FE, FC, BO, PC — trap name prefixes)
candidates.name: ORCHARD/POLYPHAGOUS x HALYOMORPHA HALYS x EMILIA-ROMAGNA (Cimice.Net, UniBO BIG / Regione E-R)
candidates.outcome_variable: Per-trap, per-weekly-inspection counts of insects captured, split into three life-stage fields exactly as served: "Adulti", "Giovani II - III (small)", "Giovani IV - V (large)". Each GeoJSON Feature also carries "name" (trap code e.g. MO29, RA31), "gid" (trap-week record id) and "installed" (epoch of trap installation). Weeks are the epoch-second keys of the top-level object.
candidates.years_claimed: 2020–2026 (7 monitoring sessions declared by getMonitoringSessionData.php)
candidates.panel_stability: VERIFIED stable-but-shrinking panel. Distinct traps per season: 2020=139, 2021=165, 2022=101, 2023=89, 2024=68, 2025=51, 2026=45. Trap-name overlap between adjacent seasons is high: 63 of 68 traps in 2024 were also present in 2023; 49 of 51 traps in 2025 were also present in 2024. So the same physical sites are re-monitored, but the network was cut by two thirds between 2020 and 2026 — a shrinking, not rotating, panel. Trap 'gid' is a per-record id and changes every year; join across years on 'name', not 'gid'.
candidates.geographic_resolution: Point lat/lon (WGS84) per individual trap, e.g. [10.70487, 44.61348] for trap MO29
candidates.temporal_resolution: Weekly (25–33 inspection weeks per season; 2024 season = 31 weeks, 2024-03-24 to 2024-10-20)
candidates.official_source: Cimice.Net — PSR Emilia-Romagna funded project; monitoring network standardised with the Settore Fitosanitario della Regione Emilia-Romagna; platform built and hosted by Università di Bologna (big.csr.unibo.it). The regional 'Bollettini di produzione integrata e biologica' are drafted using these data.
candidates.adama_relevance: H. halys is the pest that reshaped insecticide demand in Emilia-Romagna fruit growing and is a listed secondary vine pest. This is the only Italian series I could verify in this lane that gives raw, per-site, per-week insect counts with coordinates over 7 consecutive seasons at zero access cost — it is a genuine backtest target for any population/phenology component of a disease-intelligence tool, and the co-hosted weather grid removes the usual join problem. NOT a fungal pathosystem, so it does NOT substitute for the Vite x Peronospora incumbent.

lanes.lane_notes:
HEADLINE: no ITALIAN vine-disease quantitative outcome series was found in this lane beyond the already-known Toscana Vite schemas. Priority 1 (Vite x Peronospora), priority 2 (other vine disease) and priority 3 (vine pest) all came up empty for Emilia-Romagna specifically. The three candidates returned are honest second-best: one E-R insect-count network, and two Toscana AgroAmbiente siblings on other crops. I did not pad the list; a fourth entry would have been weaker than useful.

WHAT THE TOSCANA SIBLING SWEEP ACTUALLY FOUND. The API hosts exactly three crops and no more: crop=2 Olivo (15 survey schemas), crop=3 Vite (10 schemas: 4 Fenologia, 5 Tignoletta/Lobesia, 6 Muffa grigia/Botrite, 7 Peronospora, 8 Oidio, 9 Altri Insetti, 59 Acari, 77 Black Rot, 87 Cimice asiatica, 90 Tripidi), crop=19 Frumento (4 schemas). So the vine surface is fully enumerated at 10 schemas, and the only genuine siblings are olive and wheat — both reported above. Two hard operational findings for whoever harvests this: (a) years 2006–2019 are NOT retrievable — every request returns HTTP 200 with envelope ok:true but data.ok:false carrying 'SQLSTATE[42883]: Undefined function ... LEFT JOIN plus_images i ON i.guid_survey=s.id_survey'. That is a server-side type-cast bug on the images join in the older year schemas. It is ACCESS_FAILED, not zero data, and it caps every AgroAmbiente series at 2020–2026 today. (b) NO BULK EXPORT EXISTS. I probed api/dati/get_aedita_data_xls (404), api/dati/get_aedita_data_csv (404) and api/dati/export (500); the mod_aedita_dati page (HTTP 200, 18,267 bytes) references only api/dati and api/monitoring_webpack. Harvesting is a nested year x week x survey_schema loop, and difesa=all remains mandatory on every call.

EMILIA-ROMAGNA — WHAT I RULED OUT, AND WHY. (1) dati.emilia-romagna.it CKAN: queried the package_search API for fitosanitario (7 hits, all soil chemistry maps), vite (3 hits, all ISTAT farm-area statistics), peronospora (0), monitoraggio insetti (0), agrometeo (0). There is no phytosanitary monitoring dataset on the regional open-data portal. This is a verified negative, not a failure to look. (2) Regional Bollettini di produzione integrata e biologica: downloaded the Reggio Emilia bulletin n.17 of 04/06/2026 (HTTP 200, 1,097,235 bytes, 59 pages) and extracted the full text. The vine section is qualitative advisory prose only — 'Peronospora: al momento situazione di controllo della malattia buona. Monitorare la situazione', 'Oidio: presenza di sintomi occasionali'. No percentages, no counts, no denominators. Under the brief's own rule this is advisory/MODELLED_RISK, not an outcome, and I discarded it. (3) Flavescenza dorata: the regional campaign is real and large — 1,619 vineyards visited across 2023–2024 out of 1,800 selected (10% of ~18,000 regional vineyards), with visual inspection plus chromotropic traps for Scaphoideus titanus in ~120 vineyards. But the published pages give only prose ('a possible change in trend', 'no Flavescenza detected in Rimini in 2024') and I found no per-vineyard incidence figures, no trap counts and no downloadable file. This would be the single best vine candidate in the region IF the underlying data were released; as of today it is SOURCE_NOT_PUBLIC and I did not report it rather than report it on faith. Worth a direct data request to the Settore Fitosanitario. (4) Consorzio Fitosanitario Modena captaspore network: measures 'numero di ascospore di V. pyrina cumulate in due ore' on standard tape, with a season-vs-two-prior-years comparison — a genuine numeric observation, but only for melo and pero (no vine captaspore page exists), and it is published exclusively as rendered chart images with no numeric table or export. Not machine-readable, so not reported. (5) The Modena consortium's 'DIFESA PERONOSPORA DELLA VITE' page is a predictive infection model, explicitly excluded by the brief.

ON THE CIMICE.NET FIND. This was reached by reading the map application's own JavaScript rather than by search: monitoring.php -> conf/it-conf.json declares heatmap.data = './php/getHeatmapTrapsData.php?', which serves raw per-trap GeoJSON with no auth. I fetched all 7 seasons individually and counted 19,432 trap-week records. Two caveats stated plainly in the candidate: the site's own advertised download page (big.csr.unibo.it/downloads/stink-bug/) is 404, and the aggregated chart endpoint php/getChartData.php returns HTTP 500 for every parameter set I tried including with Referer/Origin/X-Requested-With headers — I am calling that ACCESS_FAILED on that one route, not evidence of missing data, because the per-trap route works perfectly. The co-hosted weather grid (getHeatmapWeatherData.php, 1,131 cells on the identical weekly keys) is base64 + RAW DEFLATE, not gzip — decompress with zlib.decompress, gzip.decompress throws BadGzipFile.

VERIFICATION DISCIPLINE. Every row count in this report is one I actually counted from a response body. I checked data.ok and data.rowCount on every AgroAmbiente call rather than trusting the HTTP code, which is what exposed the 2006–2019 SQL failure. Cross-year panel stability was measured by intersecting id_field (Toscana) and trap 'name' (Cimice.Net) between adjacent years, not assumed — and it is the weakest property of all three candidates: only 39 olive groves, 10 wheat plots and a shrinking 45-trap stink-bug network survive across all verified years.

BOTTOM LINE FOR RANKING. None of these three replaces Vite x Peronospora. Candidate 1 is the strongest dataset in raw terms (19k records, 7 years, point coords, free, weather co-located) but has no crop attribution and measures insect pressure, not disease. Candidate 2 is the strongest as an outcome variable (a true rate with n=100 denominator, plus real treatment records) and is nearly free to add to an existing Toscana harvester, but it is olive and an insect. Candidate 3 is the closest in kind to a fungal-disease backtest but is small and ordinal. If the goal is a same-pathosystem Italian benchmark, this lane says it is not publicly available in Toscana beyond what is already known, nor anywhere in Emilia-Romagna — and the highest-value next action is a formal data request to the Emilia-Romagna Settore Fitosanitario for the Flavescenza dorata per-vineyard monitoring records.

The layer abstract says the survey targets 'l'organismo nocivo Flavescenza dorata E DEL SUO VETTORE', so a positive may mean the phytoplasma OR Scaphoideus titanus was found — I did not find a field that disambiguates the two, which is a real hazard for interpretation. lanes.lane_notes:
TOP PRIORITY NOT FOUND. I found NO VITE x PERONOSPORA (Plasmopara viticola) observation series anywhere in Piemonte, Lombardia, Liguria or Valle d'Aosta. This is a verified negative, not an untested assumption:

(1) Lombardia's regional vine bulletin — I downloaded https://www.fitosanitario.regione.lombardia.it/wps/wcm/connect/11f64242-d442-476a-86c1-557390cf9017/BOLLETTINO%20REGIONALE%20VITE%20n_2_2025.pdf (HTTP 200, 857,362 bytes) and extracted all 10,922 characters of text. It contains ONLY: BBCH phenology photos, a 6-station table of rainfall mm and Tmin/Tmax (Sondrio, Montecalvo Versiggia PV, Paratico BS, San Colombano al Lambro MI, Scanzorosciate BG, Quistello MN), narrative statements that rainfall 'potrebbe aver favorito il ciclo biologico di Plasmopara viticola', and a FRAC active-substance / resistance-strategy table. Zero observed incidence, zero severity, zero trap counts. This is MODELLED_RISK plus spray advice — rain is not disease — and must not be used as ground truth.

(2) dati.lombardia.it Socrata catalog — queried the API directly at /api/catalog/v1. 'fitosanitar' = 0 results, 'popillia' = 0, 'flavescenza' = 0, 'vite' = 0, 'peronospora' = 0. The API is working, not broken: 'agricoltura' returns resultSetSize 111 and 'ersaf' returns 9 (all DUSAF land-use, forestry and pollen datasets). There is genuinely no phytosanitary outcome data on the Lombardia open-data portal — the real Lombardia phytosanitary data lives in the region's ArcGIS Online organisation (org id XannvQVnsM1hoZyv), which is how I reached candidate 2.

(3) Geoportale Piemonte — the GeoNetwork ES search API returns HTTP 403 (XSRF-protected), so I used the open CSW 2.0.2 endpoint instead: 'flavescenza' = numberOfRecordsMatched 0; 'popillia' = 0 usable records in the brief set; 'fitosanitario' = 11 records, all soil/agro-meteo cartography plus one 'Aree delimitate per la presenza di Popillia japonica'; 'vite' = 12 records, all DOC-suitability and vitigni cadastral mosaics. The single Popillia record is REGULATORY DEMARCATION POLYGONS (shapefile at datigeo-piem-download.it, WMS for 2023/2024/2025) derived from surveys, not the survey observations themselves — I deliberately did NOT promote it to a candidate because a demarcated zone is an administrative decision, not a dated field observation.

(4) dati.piemonte.it has no working CKAN action API — /api/3/action/package_search returned HTTP 404 for every query. That is an ACCESS_FAILED, not evidence of absence.

(5) Agrion (Fondazione per la ricerca l'innovazione e lo sviluppo tecnologico dell'agricoltura piemontese) does run vine trials at Carpeneto (AL) with peronospora/oidio work and is building a DSS, but I found no published quantitative outcome series — and note that an Agrion DSS output would be MODELLED_RISK anyway.

VALLE D'AOSTA: I found nothing. I did not locate any Valle d'Aosta phytosanitary observation dataset. Treat as unexplored/ACCESS_FAILED rather than empty.

ACCESS FAILURES worth re-trying with different tooling: (a) web.archive.org is blocked in this environment — curl to the CDX/snapshot endpoints returns HTTP 403 and WebFetch refuses the host — so the archived 2025 Lombardia Popillia weekly-catch page (snapshot 20260209061827 confirmed to exist via the availability API) could not be harvested. Recovering it would add a full second season of weekly per-trap data to candidate 2. (b) Earlier editions of the Piemonte Progetti Pilota synthesis (2022/2023/2024) were probed at ten guessed URL patterns, all non-200; they may exist under different paths and would materially strengthen candidate 1.

BEST BET IF ONE THING IS PURSUED: request the per-vineyard microdata behind candidate 1 directly from Regione Piemonte Settore Fitosanitario A1703B. The aggregate PDF proves 616 monitored vineyards and 10,496 traps in 2025 with a documented per-vineyard incidence and per-trap catch protocol ('Scheda registrazione adulti scafoideo' .xls and 'Metodo monitoraggio scafoideo' .pdf are both published). That microdata — vineyard-level FD incidence plus fortnightly S. titanus counts over 2022-2025 — would be a first-class backtest ground truth. Only the aggregates are public today.

SCOPE: everything reported is Italian. I did not search or retrieve any Spanish or French source, so nothing was discarded on nationality grounds.

ZERO field ids are present in all seven years. 60 comuni in total; heavily concentrated in Chieti province (2,734 of 4,127 records), then Pescara 755, Teramo 528, L'Aquila 110. 2023 is effectively a hole (17 records, 7 fields) — which is unlucky, because 2023 was the big peronospora year in central Italy.

candidates.official_source: Regione Abruzzo — portale AgroAmbiente (Servizio Fitosanitario / Agrometeorologia regionale), 'monitoraggio fitosanitario partecipato dalle aziende agricole'. candidates.adama_relevance: This is the incumbent pathosystem (vine downy mildew) in an Italian region where ADAMA Italy sells, with per-visit georeferenced observations AND the applied active substance and last treatment date on the same record (417 records carry a treatment date, 401 a product name; survey_codes list actives such as fluopicolide, folpet, ametoctradina, mandipropamide, cimoxanil, benalaxil-M). It also carries a 'difesa' regime flag (biologico / integrato / integrato volontario), so outcomes can be conditioned on management. That combination — dated georeferenced disease outcome + what was sprayed — is exactly what a backtest of a disease-intelligence tool needs, and it is rare in public Italian data.

candidates.format: Undocumented but unauthenticated JSON REST API (Drupal/'aedita' platform). One request per (crop, year, survey_schema, week); the response also leaks the underlying PostgreSQL SQL. Server-side latency ~6-7 s per call, so a full multi-year pull takes minutes, not seconds.
candidates.honest_weakness: Severe class imbalance: ~94% of records are 'nessuna' on both leaves and bunches, and the top severity classes are almost empty (3 'alta' on leaves, 6 '>15%' on bunches across seven years). Backtesting a risk model against this would mostly be testing the ability to predict zeros. The panel rotates completely — no vineyard is present in all seven years — so a fixed-site time series cannot be built without accepting large gaps, and 2023 is missing almost entirely. The outcome is ordinal, not a measured percentage (only the bunch scale carries % bands). Participation is voluntary farm/technician reporting, so absence of a record is not absence of disease, and observation effort varies by year (17 to 935 records). The API is undocumented and could change or close without notice; the same platform family is known to return HTTP 200 with rowCount 0 on a wrong parameter, so every pull must be row-checked.

Its direct commercial relevance to an ADAMA Italy disease-intelligence tool is however UNKNOWN-to-low: Xylella is a quarantine bacterium managed by eradication and vector control, not by a fungicide programme, and the crop is olive rather than vine.

candidates.honest_weakness: Wrong crop and wrong kind of pathosystem for the incumbent use case: a vector-borne quarantine bacterium, not a weather-driven foliar disease, so a seasonal weather-to-disease model has little to predict here. More importantly the sampling is REGULATORY and TARGETED — inspectors sample where the demarcated zones and buffer strips require it, so the positive rate is a function of where they chose to look, not of ambient disease pressure; the 2020→2022 collapse in positives (2,006 → 242) partly reflects survey redesign and zone shifts, not only epidemiology. The panel is not stable (only 15 of 106 comuni sampled in all four years) and 2023 is a partial campaign (91,109 samples, 25 comuni). No treatment/defence information at all. The catalogue advertises 2020-2022 while the file holds 2020-2023, and the newer CAMP_2020_2023.csv resource has no working download URL, so the update path is unclear.
