lanes.lane_notes:
MAIN FIND. The Abruzzo AgroAmbiente portal (agroambiente.regione.abruzzo.it) exposes an UNDOCUMENTED but UNAUTHENTICATED JSON read API at /api/dati/get_aedita_data. I found it by reading the inline script of the public page /mod_aedita_dati_p?type=aep, which sets var dati_api_path='api/dati' (the authenticated sibling /mod_aedita_dati returns 403; the public one does not). Required parameters: crop, year, survey_schema, tipo_elab=storic_map, week (a week value is MANDATORY — omitting it returns rowCount null and no rows). This is the same 'aedita' platform family as the Toscana AgroAmbiente system, and it shows exactly the failure mode I was warned about: it happily returns HTTP 200 with ok:true and rowCount 0 for a wrong parameter combination, so I row-checked every pull. It also leaks the underlying PostgreSQL query in the response, which is how I confirmed what is being selected. Server-side latency is ~6-7 s per call.

WHAT ELSE IS IN THE ABRUZZO API BEYOND THE TWO CANDIDATES I RANKED. crop=3 (Vite) has ten survey schemas: Fenologia (122), Peronospora (7), Oidio (8), Botrite (6), Marciumi (123), Lobesia (5), Tignola rigata (74), Altri Insetti (9), Danni da fisiopatia (110), Maturazione uva (72). I harvested Oidio in full as well and did not report it as a separate candidate only to avoid spending a slot on a near-duplicate of the peronospora structure: VERIFIED 4,037 oidio observation rows, 2020-2026 (2020=618, 2021=581, 2022=393, 2023=16, 2024=918, 2025=755, 2026=756), 169 fields, 60 comuni, weeks 12-40, with 4,000 non-null 'presenza attiva su foglie', 3,927 'presenza attiva su grappoli', 408 treatment dates and 386 products. If the team wants a second vine DISEASE rather than a vine pest in slot 2, Oidio Abruzzo is available on identical terms and is already verified. crop=2 (Olivo) additionally offers 'Catture mosca dell'olivo' (schema 5) with a numeric 'media_catture' field and 'Punture mosca dell'olivo' (schema 99) — I did not harvest these, so they are unverified.

CANDIDATE I DROPPED TO FIFTH — LAZIO OLIVE FLY, and it is genuinely usable if a fifth slot ever opens. OP LATIUM / Servizio Fitosanitario Regionale del Lazio publish weekly per-zone 'Bollettino Fitosanitario' PDFs for Bactrocera oleae at agroambientelazio.it. These are real observations with a stated sampling protocol: 'Si esaminano 20 olive a pianta su 10 piante scelte a caso per cultivar per ettaro, un totale di 200 olive', reported as 'RILIEVO INFESTAZIONE — Attacco rilevato: X%'. VERIFIED by downloading and reading three PDFs: /public/news_file/202608251215040.pdf (HTTP 200, 385,623 bytes, zone SABINA, week 24-30/08/2026, 'Attacco rilevato: 0-1%'), /public/news_file/202509230943051.pdf (HTTP 200, 393,396 bytes, zone VETRALLA, 22-29/09/2025, 'Attacco rilevato: 2-5%') and /public/news_file/202509230943053.pdf (HTTP 200, 393,627 bytes, zone VITERBO INTERNA — Tuscania/Canino/Cellere/Tessennano, same week, 'Attacco rilevato: 2-5%'). So: 2 years verified (2025, 2026), 3 actual observation values read, 5 zones per week, ~200 news items in the archive going back to at least Aug 2020 (news id 150 = 'Bollettino Avvertimento Fitopatologico n. 3/2020 Mosca dell'olivo'). Weakness: one bracketed number per zone per week, no coordinates, and older news pages did not expose PDF links to me, so historical depth is claimed but not verified.

WHAT I CHECKED AND REJECTED, with reasons.
1) BILANCIO FITOSANITARIO (AIPP / Giornate Fitopatologiche / Servizi Fitosanitari Regionali), vine centro-sud. I initially rated this highly and then downgraded it after reading the actual PDFs. The MARCHE deck (giornatefitopatologiche.it .../Bilancio-Vite-Marche-2020---2021.pdf, HTTP 200 after setting a browser User-Agent, 4,971,851 bytes, 40 pages) DOES use a structured template with real observations — e.g. 2020 peronospora: 'Presenza dei primi sintomi: metà giugno 2020; Vitigno: Verdicchio; BBCH 75; Organo colpito: foglie; Gravità dell'attacco: irrilevante (<5% delle foglie con comparsa di sintomi); Sito: Monsano (AN)', and the same template for 2021 and for oidio ('irrilevante-bassa, <10% dei grappoli'). But the PUGLIA deck for the same series (aipp.it/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Puglia-Vite-2023.pdf, HTTP 200, 2,263,759 bytes, 25 pages) is PURELY NARRATIVE — a 2022-vs-2023 table of prose per adversity ('Gestione agevole' / 'Gestione problematica'), with no severity class, no percentage, no site. The template is therefore NOT consistent between regions, so this cannot be assembled into a numeric region x year x disease panel; it is at best a hand-coded qualitative annual label, one point per region per year. Also note the Marche deck's charts are vite.net DSS model output (oospore dose, infection index) — MODELLED_RISK, and using those would be scoring a model against a model. Note the giornatefitopatologiche.it index pages are behind CloudFront and return 403 to a default UA; the PDFs themselves fetch fine with a browser UA, and the full archive index is reachable at giornatefitopatologiche.it/it/altri-eventi/8/... (HTTP 200, 27,135 bytes) listing per-region vine decks for Abruzzo, Calabria, Puglia, Sardegna, Sicilia (uva da tavola), Toscana and Umbria for 2022-2023.
2) ALSIA / Basilicata, 'Il bilancio fitosanitario della vite ad uva da tavola in Basilicata nel triennio 2020-2022'. Fetched and read: NO field quantities at all. The only numbers are 475 ha of cultivated area, 70% late production, ~30% organic, 17 regulated pest species, plus a phenology remark that the 2021 second Lobesia flight was about a month late. No trap catches, no incidence, no severity. Rejected — a lexical mention of monitoring is not an occurrence.
3) Campania. The Servizio Fitosanitario Regionale runs a real UTM-based monitoring network and states that bulletins report 'lo stato fitosanitario delle diverse colture rilevati nelle aziende di riferimento (Unità territoriali di monitoraggio - UTM)', weekly 1 March - 30 September, per province (AV, BN, CE, NA, SA). Index pages fetched OK (agricoltura.regione.campania.it/difesa/rete.html HTTP 200 27,905 bytes; .../bollettini/bollettini_2026.html HTTP 200 10,903 bytes) but the PDF links are injected dynamically and I extracted ZERO pdf hrefs, so I could not open a single bulletin. Status is ACCESS_FAILED, NOT 'no data' — this is the most promising unchecked lead left in this lane and deserves a second pass with a different fetch strategy.
4) Marche AMAP/ASSAM. The agrometeo service clearly runs a phenological/epidemiological monitoring network and publishes weekly Notiziari, but I found no structured data endpoint and did not verify any observation rows. UNVERIFIED, not rejected.
5) Puglia beyond Xylella. I queried the Puglia CKAN catalogue (package_search for fitosanitario/monitoraggio/xylella/vite, HTTP 200) and it returns exactly ONE dataset — the Xylella one. There is no open vine monitoring dataset there. The Puglia SIT ArcGIS server (webapps.sit.puglia.it/arcgis/rest/services, HTTP 200) exists but I did not need it once the CSV worked.
6) Abruzzo weekly bulletins as a text source. Readable (nodes 411, 425, 639, 674, 683 all HTTP 200) and they do contain occasional real numbers, e.g. downy mildew 'diffusione e danno stimato circa 10%' in the Vastese — but they explicitly push the detailed trap data to the app ('per dati dettagliati vedi VISUALIZZA MONITORAGGIO SU APP'), which is precisely the API I ended up using directly. No reason to parse the prose.

SCOPE. I searched only Italian sources. Nothing Spanish or French was retrieved, ranked or discarded — the non_italian_discarded list is empty because no non-Italian series entered the pipeline at all.

REPRODUCIBILITY. Harvest scripts and raw pulls are at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-eame-sintonia/225e1b33-2ad9-51d4-af35-56626f84e287/scratchpad/ (h2.py + abr_pero.json for peronospora; h3.py + abr_lob_oid.json for Lobesia and Oidio; h2.out and h3.out hold the counts quoted above). The Puglia CSV is at /tmp/xf_camp.csv (82 MB).

ADAMA and its competitors themselves contribute trials to this corpus, so the format and quality are familiar to the Italian team.

lanes.lane_notes:
WHAT THIS LANE ACTUALLY CONTAINS: the Italian national level publishes almost no machine-readable phytosanitary OUTCOME data. That is a verified finding, not a guess, and it is the single most useful thing this lane returns.

dati.gov.it CKAN sweep (all HTTP 200, real JSON parsed, counts are what the API returned): q=fitosanitar -> 0 packages; q=fitosanitario -> 38, none of which is a disease-outcome series (they are export phytosanitary certificates, authorisations, municipal street-tree condition); q=peronospora -> 0; q=flavescenza -> 0; q="cimice asiatica" -> 0; q=Popillia -> 0; q=avversita -> 0; q="bollettino fitosanitario" -> 0; q=fitopatologic -> 0; q=vite -> 10, all land-use/registry, no disease; q="organismi nocivi" -> 4; q="monitoraggio fitosanitario" -> 6; q=Xylella -> 2; q=trappole -> 7 (Ips typographus forest traps, carabid beetles, rodenticide baits — nothing on vine). The entire national catalogue yields exactly two usable phytosanitary outcome datasets, and BOTH are Regione Puglia's, merely harvested into the national catalogue. There is no CREA, ISTAT, MASAF, SIAN, Agrit or ISPRA disease-outcome dataset in dati.gov.it that I could find.

WHY THE NATIONAL SURVEY DATA IS NOT THERE: the Piano Nazionale di Indagine (PNI, Reg. EU 2016/2031) is the one nationally-mandated, numerically-structured phytosanitary observation system in Italy. Its results are transmitted annually to the European Commission, not published as national open data. PNI plan documents for 2020, 2022, 2023 and 2024 exist on protezionedellepiante.it; the RESULTS do not. Puglia is the only region I found that publishes its own return (708 rows, 2024, EU template, verified). If ADAMA Italy wants national coverage, the realistic route is an institutional request to MASAF Servizio Fitosanitario Centrale for the PNI returns, not a scrape.

ACCESS FAILURES — these are failures, NOT zeros. www.protezionedellepiante.it (the national Servizio Fitosanitario Nazionale portal, the single most likely home for national surveillance numbers) could not be retrieved at all: WebFetch returned HTTP 503 twice, and curl failed TLS chain verification three times (curl error 60) even with --cacert /root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt and with CURL_CA_BUNDLE set. I never saw its /sorveglianza/ page body. Do not conclude it holds nothing — it is UNASSESSED. www.giornatefitopatologiche.it returned HTTP 403 CloudFront 'Request blocked' on every path (/it/, /it/atti, /it/ricerca, /it/download/23?tok=...) via both curl and WebFetch, so I could not enumerate or count the vine/peronospora trial papers in the national Atti archive; my candidate 2 rests on a single author-hosted reprint. Both sites are worth retrying from a different egress or a real browser — candidate 2 in particular could be far stronger than I was able to demonstrate.

NOT CHECKED, SO NOT CLAIMED: I did not query ISTAT's API, the Agrit sampling survey, Rete Rurale Nazionale or ISPRA directly. My expectation is that ISTAT/Agrit carry crop area and production but no disease outcome, and ISPRA carries pesticide residues in water rather than disease, but I did NOT verify this and I am not asserting it as a finding. EPPO Global Database filtered to Italy was also not fetched; note in advance that EPPO records are distribution/status statements, not dated repeated observations, so even a successful fetch would likely fail the outcome test.

ONE STRONG SERIES THAT BELONGS TO ANOTHER LANE: the CREA 2024 proceedings document a Veneto flavescenza dorata monitoring exercise run in 2024 on 'lo stesso campione di 3.065 particelle vitate già esaminate nel 2023' — 2.792.208 plants, 42 varieties, ~900 ha, 176 comuni, with mean incidence falling from 3–5% (2022) to 1–2% (2024) on Glera, Pinot grigio, Garganega and Chardonnay. That is an explicitly STABLE PANEL across at least two years on the exact crop of interest, which is rarer than anything else I saw. I could only verify it as a secondary description inside the CREA PDF; the underlying Veneto dataset is a regional asset and should be chased hard by the Veneto lane.

RANKING LOGIC, STATED PLAINLY: candidate 1 (CREA proceedings) leads on crop and pathosystem fit and on being a genuinely repeating annual official publication, but it is prose, not data. Candidate 2 is the only thing in this lane that is literally VITE x PERONOSPORA with dated numeric untreated-control readings AND matched defence data, but it is a scattered corpus with no index and its archive blocked me. Candidate 3 is, by an enormous margin, the best-engineered dataset (688.631 georeferenced dated sample-level rows, 4 years) and the worst crop fit (olive, zero vine rows) — I ranked it third rather than first precisely because data quality must not outrank relevance. Candidate 4 is included as an institutional lead, not as a usable series, and I would not object to it being dropped.

FINALLY: nothing in this lane is a drop-in backtest ground truth. The honest summary for the parent is that national-level Italy gives you (a) high-quality annual vine disease numbers locked inside CREA PDFs, (b) a rich but unindexed national trial corpus behind a bot block, and (c) excellent georeferenced data for the wrong crop. The genuinely national, numeric, vine-disease panel does not appear to exist in public form.

_skeptic.notes:
VERDICT: I could not refute this. It is Italian (Regione del Veneto, U.O. Fitosanitario), it is a genuine repeated dated field observation, and I personally retrieved THREE distinct years from primary official documents - one more than the hunter claimed.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF (primary documents, not citations):
- 2026 turno 1 (bull. n.16, 22/07/2026): 468 traps, 156 vineyards, 42% bio / 78% conv below threshold, 16% unacceptable.
- 2026 turno 2 (bull. n.18, 06/08/2026): 471 traps, 157 vineyards, 38% bio / 76% conv.
- 2025 turno 1 (bull. n.16, 23/07/2025): 477 traps, 159 vineyards, 35% bio / 68% conv.
- 2024 turno 1 (24/07/2024, inline HTML): 477 traps, 159 vineyards, 41% bio / 84% integrata.
- 2024 turno 2 (07/08/2024, inline HTML): 55% overall absent-or-minimal, 40% bio / 59% conv.
=> 5 turno-level reporting events across 3 years. 2023 (77%/93%) and 2022 (38%/75%) were read ONLY as citations inside the 2024 bulletin, so I do not count them.

THE MODEL ATTACK FAILS OUTRIGHT. This is not agrometeo model output. It is physical yellow sticky traps (mod. Glutor 40x25 cm), 3 per vineyard, swapped and counted by technicians on a fixed fortnightly turno. Nothing in the variable is simulated. Circularity risk is genuinely NONE.

THE HUNTER MATERIALLY UNDERSTATED THE DATA. Its 'honest_weakness' says the public product is only 'due-tre percentuali per turno' at regional aggregate. That is wrong. I rendered page 7 of the 2026 PDF at 150 dpi and read it: the bulletin publishes a GEOREFERENCED POINT MAP, one symbol per monitored vineyard over a Veneto basemap with province labels, binned into six catch classes (0, <2, 3-9, 10-29, 30-99, >100), split bio vs conventional, WITH per-class counts printed in the legend - and the prior year's map printed beneath it for comparison. That is ~157 site-level ordinal observations per mapped turno (I read 157 for 2026 and 157 for 2025 = 314 site classifications). Site coordinates are recoverable to a few km by digitising the points, so 'weather_join_feasible: NO' and 'geographic_resolution: aggregato regionale' are both too pessimistic. A weather join is laborious, not infeasible.

INDEPENDENT ARITHMETIC VALIDATION (2026 reconciles exactly): bio 26 = 8+3+3+5+3+4; below threshold (8+3)/26 = 42.3% = the stated 42%. conv 131 = 78+25+15+5+4+4; (78+25)/131 = 78.6% = the stated 78%. Unacceptable (classes >=10) = 12 bio + 13 conv = 25/157 = 15.9% = the stated 16%. Three independent checks pass. That is strong evidence the published aggregates are honest reductions of real site data.

THE ONE THING THAT DOES NOT RECONCILE: the 2025 conventional figure. The 2025 bulletin prose says 68%. The same 2025 turno-1 map reprinted in the 2026 bulletin gives 0[68] + <2[32] of [131] = 76.3%. The bio figure reconciles (34.6% -> 35%) but the conventional one is off by 8 points. Note the suspicious coincidence that 68 is exactly the class-0 count. Either the 2025 prose was wrong, or the series was silently re-cut. Anyone backtesting must use the map class counts, not the prose percentages.

OTHER REAL LIMITS: only ~2 observation events per season are published (n.19 and n.20 of Aug 2026 carry no monitoring section at all - the hunter's 'fortnightly through end September' is wrong); the 2022/2023 seasons are 404 on the live site and Wayback was ACCESS_FAILED through this proxy (403 / connection reset), so 2023 may well be recoverable elsewhere; the vineyard list is unpublished so panel identity cannot be audited from outside; stratum label drifted from 'integrata' (2024) to 'convenzionale' (2025-26); denominators wobble between prose and map within the same PDF (156 vs 157, 159 vs 157); and there is no CSV or API - everything requires PDF text extraction plus raster point digitisation.

OUTCOME TYPE: PERCENTAGE is correct as the hunter labelled it - the headline variable is the share of monitored vineyards falling below a trap-catch threshold. Worth noting the underlying site-level datum is an ordinal binned COUNT (adults per 3 traps per fortnight), which is the more useful form if anyone digitises the maps.

SCOPE: fully Italian, nothing Spanish or French touched. Andalucia RAIF not consulted.

lanes.lane_notes:
WHAT THE LANE ACTUALLY YIELDED. The structural finding is that Italy has plenty of real vine monitoring networks, but almost none of them publish the observations as data. The observations exist — 477 traps across 159 vineyards, 2.79 million vines walked for flavescenza, named untreated control plots scored through the epidemic — and they are described, sometimes with numbers, in annual PDF proceedings and weekly bulletins. What is published is the narrative summary. The row-level records sit with the regional Servizi Fitosanitari and are not open. The one genuine exception I found is Puglia, and it is on olive.

THE ANNUAL AIPP / GIORNATE FITOPATOLOGICHE 'BILANCIO FITOSANITARIO' CYCLE is the highest-value entry point I found and I would flag it to the parent as the thing to pull on. It is a recurring national event (northern-Italy proceedings published by CREA Viticoltura ed Enologia at Conegliano; centre/south decks hosted on aipp.it), where each Regional Phytosanitary Service presents its season with, in several cases, actual numbers from untreated control plots and monitoring panels. I verified the 2021 and 2024 CREA proceedings and the 2023 and 2025 Umbria decks. Editions for 2022, 2023 and 2025 (northern Italy) are referenced but I did NOT retrieve them, so I have not claimed them. Assembling that archive would give a multi-region, multi-year, hand-extractable ground-truth compendium — the single most efficient move available in this lane.

HORTA / VITE.NET — RULED OUT AS GROUND TRUTH, AND IT IS A CONTAMINATION HAZARD. Everything Vite.net publishes that I could see is model output: infection risk for peronospora, botrite, oidio and black rot, updated hourly, driven by temperature, rainfall and leaf wetness, presented as a colour-coded risk level. That is MODELLED_RISK by the brief's own definition and scoring an engine against it would be scoring a model against a model. Worse, it leaks: the Regione Umbria 2025 AIPP deck places a 'DSS peronospora 2025 (Vite.net)' slide adjacent to its real untreated-plot scorings. The same hazard applies to Emilia-Romagna's DOWGRAPRI (a Plasmopara infection simulation built by the ER and Piemonte phytosanitary services with the Universities of Piacenza and Bologna) and to the risk narrative woven through the Veneto bulletins. Any extraction from these documents must be sentence-level and hand-checked.

UNIVERSITY/CONSORTIUM ANGLE — PARTIALLY CONFIRMED, NOT CONVERTED. The lane hypothesis (universities feeding observations into networks, as 'unipi' does in Toscana) is real: DOWGRAPRI is a Piacenza/Bologna collaboration, CREA Conegliano runs its own untreated Glera plots at Spresiano (TV), and in Trentino the monitoring teams of the Cantine sociali and the Consorzio tutela vini del Trentino covered more than 6,100 ha in 2024 alongside the provincial service — a genuine consorzio di tutela contributing field observations at scale. But I found no consorzio, university or DSS company publishing its observation rows. The Trentino consorzio figure is reported only as 'about half the mean number of symptomatic vines per hectare compared with 2023', which is a ratio, not a series. The Consorzio Fitosanitario Provinciale di Reggio Emilia (fitosanitario.re.it, both pages HTTP 200, 34,587 and 49,228 bytes, read in full) publishes a long-running annual notiziario with a dedicated peronospora/oidio review and runs its own agrometeo network at fitoclimate.fitosanitario.re.it — but its disease reporting is almost entirely qualitative prose (the only numbers are intervention counts, '15 interventi', and one giallumi delta of '-1; -1,5%'), so it did not make the candidate list.

ACCESS FAILURES — THESE ARE NOT ZEROES. This is a technician recording what he saw on a visit, which is exactly what the brief calls a valid outcome. The tignole trap catches in Carso 2024 and 2026 are hard COUNTs at named stations (Sagrado 3, Prepotto 5 in 2026).

BUT the circularity risk the hunter rated MEDIUM is real and I confirmed it in the document body: Carso n.5/2024 prints 'I modelli previsionali danno possibili infezioni con medio rischio' three times, once directly beneath each of the peronospora, oidio and black rot observation lines. Model and observation are adjacent, same font, same section. They are lexically separable, but only by a parser built deliberately to separate them. Get that wrong and the backtest scores a model against a model.

THE REAL LIMITS, WHICH ARE EXTRACTION LIMITS RATHER THAN VALIDITY LIMITS. (1) 2016-2017 is materially weaker than 2020-2026: the 2016 peronospora section is favourable-conditions language plus a REGIONAL pressure statement, not a Carso rilievo. (2) A naive pathogen-keyword extractor will actively produce a WRONG series from the 2020 layout, because the only paragraph headed 'Peronospora' there is spray advice while the real observation sits in an unnamed block. (3) Carso 2021 embeds a regional '>50% delle osservazioni' beside the zone observation - a spatial misattribution trap. (4) Filename years are corrupt: I fetched a file named ..._N_5_DEL_2024_ZONA_DOC_CARSO.pdf whose body reads 'N. 5 DEL 8 MAGGIO 2026'. Key the panel on the PDF body date or the upload prefix, never the filename. (5) The vineyard panel is never enumerated in any of the nine PDFs, so there is no denominator and no incidence for most zone-weeks.

OUTCOME TYPE. The hunter labelled it PRESENCE and that is correct - I did not need to change it. The dominant, continuously available variable is a dated presence/absence-of-new-infection statement per zone-week. Occasional percentages appear (2017 '30% dei vigneti trattati', 2021 '>50% delle osservazioni') but with inconsistent denominators and inconsistent spatial scope, so they cannot be promoted to a clean INCIDENCE series.

VERDICT. Survives as a weak-but-legitimate ground truth: a binary/ordinal PRESENCE-of-new-infection target at DOC-zone by ISO-week, roughly 6 zones x ~15-20 weeks x 11+ seasons, plus a genuinely numeric COUNT sub-series for tignole at named stations in recent years. It is not numeric, not coded, and needs a careful sentence-level NLP extractor with an observation/model/advice classifier. Usable for backtesting whether a tool flagged risk in the weeks a technician actually recorded new infections. It is NOT usable for severity or incidence calibration.

Scope compliance: nothing non-Italian was searched, fetched, or considered.

_skeptic.candidate_name: ORCHARD/POLYPHAGOUS x HALYOMORPHA HALYS x EMILIA-ROMAGNA (Cimice.Net, UniBO BIG / Regione E-R)
refutation_grounds: NOT REFUTED on the core claim. I independently re-fetched all 7 seasons and reproduced the hunter's headline numbers exactly (19,432 rows; per-season trap/week counts; panel overlaps 63/68 for 2024 and 49/51 for 2025). Grounds below are CORRECTIONS that survive as caveats, not disqualifications.

CORRECTION 1 (material, hunter's claim is FALSE): 'Co-hosted gridded weather on the SAME weekly keys as the trap data' is wrong. I decoded the prec_day grid for msId=14 (base64 + raw DEFLATE, 0x78da, 31 weekly grids x 1,131 polygon cells) and the EXACT intersection of trap week keys with weather week keys is ZERO. Trap keys are local Italian wall-clock (e.g. 1711321200 = 2024-03-24 23:00 UTC = 2024-03-25 00:00 CET); weather keys are UTC midnight (1711324800). The offset is NOT constant: it is 3600s or 7200s depending on DST. A naive key join returns 0 rows. The join is still feasible after DST-aware date normalization, so weather_join_feasible stays YES, but it was asserted as verified when a direct join in fact fails.

CORRECTION 2 (observation count inflated ~9%): 1,690 of the 19,432 rows are placeholder rows in which every life-stage field is null (no inspection recorded), not observations. Real non-null trap-week observations = 17,742. Per season all-null rows: 2020=210, 2021=575, 2022=248, 2023=231, 2024=156, 2025=189, 2026=81.

CORRECTION 3 (schema not uniform, contra 'three life-stage fields exactly as served'): msId=6 (2020) additionally carries 'Ovature' and 'Ovatura schiusa' (egg-mass fields) that exist in NO other season. Every season also carries an undocumented 'new' boolean (present on 138 of 2,108 rows in 2024). Any cross-year panel must reconcile a 5-field 2020 against a 3-field 2021-2026.

CORRECTION 4 (phantom week): msId=6 (2020) has an extra top-level key that is the EMPTY STRING '' holding 139 all-null features. A loader doing sorted(keys, key=int) crashes on 2020. Real 2020 = 25 numeric weeks.

CORRECTION 5 (panel overlap cherry-picked): the hunter quoted only the two strongest adjacent pairs (2023->2024 = 63/68 = 93%, 2024->2025 = 49/51 = 96%). The weakest transition is 2022->2023 at 63/89 = 71%, and 2020->2021 is 136/165 = 82%. The panel is still stable-and-shrinking as described, but continuity across the 2022/2023 break is materially worse than advertised.

CORRECTION 6 (year count soft): 2026 (msId=16) is an INCOMPLETE, in-progress season - 23 weeks ending 2026-08-30 against a declared end of 2026-08-31, and today is 2026-09-06. Only 6 seasons (2020-2025) are complete. sum_Adulti for 2026 is 3,174 vs 13,722-39,785 in full seasons, so including it unadjusted would bias any trend.

SCOPE CAVEAT (not a refutation): this is a PEST population/phenology series, not a disease series. Trap catch is explicitly admitted as an outcome type by the task definition ('counts, trap catches'), and the hunter is honest that it does not substitute for a fungal pathosystem. But it delivers NO incidence, NO severity, NO % fruit injured - it cannot backtest a disease-damage model, only a population-pressure/phenology component.

_skeptic.notes:
VERDICT: SURVIVES. I attacked this hard and could not refute the core claim. All numbers independently reproduced.

ITALIAN: Yes, unambiguously. Emilia-Romagna (provinces MO, RA, FE, FC, BO, PC confirmed from trap-name prefixes in the payload I parsed), hosted by Universita di Bologna (big.csr.unibo.it), funded by PSR Emilia-Romagna, Italian-language UI ("Numero medio di cimici", "Trappole"). Not Spanish, not French.

OBSERVATION-vs-MODEL (the hardest attack, and it FAILS to disqualify): I specifically suspected the endpoint name "getHeatmapTrapsData" meant server-side kriging/interpolation, which would have made this MODELLED output. It does not. Evidence: (a) every one of the ~6,300 life-stage values I scanned in msId=14 is a pure integer string - ZERO values contain a decimal point; (b) the distribution is heavily zero-inflated (3,109 zeros vs 430 ones vs 314 twos, long tail to 320) which is a raw count signature, not a smoothed field; (c) values sit at exact fixed point coordinates carrying a physical trap code (MO29, RA31) and an "installed" epoch, with zero traps changing coordinates within a season; (d) each record carries a per-record "gid". Contrast this directly with the WEATHER layer from the same host, which IS an interpolated product - continuous floats like "38.0000057220459" on ~0.063x0.045 deg Polygon cells. The two layers are structurally different, and only the weather one is modelled. The outcome variable here is a physical count of insects removed from a pheromone trap by a technician on a dated weekly visit. That is ground truth.

OUTCOME_TYPE: COUNT is CORRECT as labelled - no correction needed. It is a per-trap, per-week integer capture count, split by life stage. It is emphatically NOT incidence, NOT severity, NOT a percentage, NOT an ordinal presence class.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF: all 7 seasons fetched individually (msId 6/9/12/13/14/15/16), all HTTP 200 with 237KB-1.22MB real payloads, parsed and row-counted. 19,432 total feature rows, of which 17,742 carry at least one non-null count. Nonzero-catch rate 70-79% per season, so the series has genuine signal and is not a wall of zeros. Weekly cadence 23-33 weeks/season. No API key, no cookie, no referer required. Requested 6 complete seasons + 1 in progress - well past the 3-year bar.

MATERIAL CORRECTIONS (see refutation_grounds for detail): the weather "same weekly keys" claim is factually FALSE (zero exact key intersection, DST-varying 1-2h offset; join needs date normalization); observation count is ~9% inflated by all-null placeholder rows; the 2020 season has a non-numeric empty-string week key that will crash a naive loader and carries two extra egg-mass fields no other year has; panel-overlap stats were quoted from the two best pairs only (worst adjacent transition is 71%, not 93-96%); and 2026 is a partial open season.

CONFIRMED HONEST: every weakness the hunter self-declared checked out. getChartData.php really does return HTTP 500 with an empty body (ACCESS_FAILED, not absence). /downloads/stink-bug/ really is 404. Crop attribution really is absent - I probed for an alternate getTrapsData.php endpoint hoping to find it and got 404, and grepped the front-end and config for coltura/crop/pero/pesco/frutteto with zero hits. No licence statement exists anywhere on the host, so redistribution terms are genuinely UNKNOWN - that is a real legal risk for a commercial product, though not a data-quality refutation.

BIGGEST REAL LIMITATION for the stated purpose: this is a pest-population series, not a disease series. It gives population pressure and phenology, never damage - no incidence, no severity, no % fruit injured, and no treatment/defence data, so you cannot distinguish genuinely low pressure from a sprayed block. It can backtest a phenology/population component of a disease-intelligence tool and nothing more. The hunter states this plainly and does not oversell it as a Peronospora substitute, which I credit.

OUTCOME TYPE: hunter's COUNT is correct for the primary variable — media_catture is mean adult catches per pheromone trap, a count-scale abundance measure. The honest backtest is the 2024-2026 era, 27 fields observed in all three seasons, ~2,091 records, weekly, georeferenced to point lat/lon — joinable to the regional agrometeo network for a degree-day / flight-phenology scoring exercise. 2. It is a corpus, not a series. The hunter is right and this is structural. No fixed plots, re-sited every season, so no per-location time series is constructible. The best continuity I found was within a single paper (same Pianella vineyard 2016 and 2017).

3. Geolocation and cadence are worse than claimed. Contract CROs (Agrea, Sagea, Agri2000) report only 'in provincia di Verona / Cuneo / Ravenna' — province, not municipality — which is too coarse for an honest Plasmopara weather join. And the 2022 tables give ONE dated rilievo per site-season, not the '2 to 5 controlli' the hunter generalised from the 2013 specimen. Partial mitigation: paper 5746 publishes its own per-trial rainfall (mm and events >5mm over the trial window), so some papers carry usable weather in-band.

4. Extraction cost is far higher than 'hand-normalising PDFs'. The archive PDFs embed 20+ subsetted CFF fonts with no ToUnicode CMap, so text extraction returns ciphertext. 2018 files are a uniform +29 shift and decode cleanly. 2022 files use an arbitrary per-file glyph-order substitution in which the DIGITS are remapped with no linguistic redundancy to crack them against — a cipher-solving harvester would emit silently wrong numbers, which is the worst possible failure for ground truth. I had to render pages to PNG and read them visually. Budget OCR, not parsing. Note the VitEn author reprint extracted cleanly, so author-hosted reprints are cheaper than the official copies where they exist.

TWO TRAPS FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THE HARVESTER:
- The entire 2008 edition returns HTTP 200 + application/pdf + 0 bytes (12/12 sampled). Every other edition 1998-2024 serves real PDFs. An unguarded loop would record 2008 as 'no trials'. Assert size_download > 0 and that the body starts with %PDF. Mark 2008 ACCESS_FAILED, never zero.
- Keyword harvesting on 'peronospora'/'Plasmopara' WILL pull in MODELLED_RISK papers — I found 2008 id 3892 'andamento delle epidemie di Plasmopara viticola e valutazione del modello...' and 2014 id 4370 on the vite.net DSS. Per-paper triage is mandatory; the discriminator is whether a physically-sampled untreated control table exists.

CIRCULARITY: genuinely NONE. These are pre-registration field trials run by CROs and manufacturers, independent of any agrometeo DSS, which is exactly what you want in a backtest reference.

SCOPE: Italy only throughout. Nothing Spanish or French was searched, used, or counted; the Andalucia RAIF XML dumps sitting in the shared scratchpad are another lane's and are excluded as instructed.

RECOMMENDED USE: not as a risk-model backtest series — the siting bias, saturation and absence of true negatives forbid that. Use it as (a) a defence-effect reference, where the treated-vs-untreated contrast with fully documented product, dose and application dates is its real and rare strength, and (b) a coarse per-region seasonal-conduciveness corroborator. Realistic yield after triage: on the order of 5-9 vine-peronospora papers per biennial edition across ~13 usable editions, each carrying 1-6 site-seasons.

_skeptic.candidate_name: VITE x FLAVESCENZA DORATA/GIALLUMI x VENETO (monitoraggio massivo, Servizio Fitosanitario Regionale)
refutation_grounds: ONLY ONE YEAR OF THE CANDIDATE'S OWN OUTCOME IS RETRIEVABLE. I downloaded both PDFs the hunter cited (both HTTP 200, real PDFs, text extracted with pymupdf). The 2024 proceedings contain the Veneto mass-survey paragraph verbatim as claimed. The 2021 proceedings contain NO Veneto giallumi number at all: I grepped every '%' character in the entire Veneto section (lines 313-471 of the extracted text, from 'Andamento delle principali malattie nell'annata viticola 2021 in Veneto' to the FVG heading at line 476) and there are ZERO percent signs. The Veneto 2021 section is pure narrative ('preoccupante recrudescenza dei sintomi'). So n_years for the candidate panel = 1 (2024), not 2.

THE HUNTER MISATTRIBUTED THE 2021 NUMBER TO THE WRONG REGION. The '237 vigneti / 1,17% viti sintomatiche' figure sits at line 610 of the 2021 text, inside the section 'Bilancio fitosanitario della vite 2021 in Friuli-Venezia Giulia' (heading at line 476, ERSA authors Bressan/Mutton). It is a DIFFERENT network in a DIFFERENT region, not evidence that the Veneto panel reported in 2021.

THE 2022 VENETO VALUE DOES NOT COME FROM THIS PANEL. Regione del Veneto's own 2026 press release (articleId=14384902, HTTP 200) states 'Il monitoraggio 2026 rappresenta la quarta annualita consecutiva di raccolta sistematica dei dati sul territorio' -> systematic collection = 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026. The '3-5% del 2022' quoted in the 2024 proceedings therefore predates the 3.065-parcel panel and is a retrospective, unsourced recollection, not a measurement on the stable sample. The stable-panel claim is verifiable only for 2023->2024, and I never retrieved the 2023 report itself.

EVERYTHING PUBLISHED IS A BAND, NOT A VALUE. The only Veneto incidence figures in existence publicly are 'dal 3-5% del 2022 all'1-2% rilevato nel 2024' and a relative '-5,5%' change in territorial diffusion. A 1-2% band is a factor-2 interval covering the whole region and 176 comuni; it cannot serve as a backtest target. Zero per-comune, per-parcel, per-variety or per-date values are published anywhere I could reach. That is at most one fuzzy interval per region per year.

NO OPEN DATA EXISTS AND THE ONE PLAUSIBLE HOST IS UNREACHABLE. dati.gov.it CKAN package_search?q=flavescenza returned HTTP 200 with success:true and count:0 and results:[] (a genuine zero, the exact 200-but-empty failure mode). dati.veneto.it/api/3/action/package_search returned HTTP 404 with a Liferay HTML error page - there is no CKAN there at all. www.avepa.it/monitoraggio-flavescenza-dorata failed twice with curl exit 35 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' and HTTP 503 via WebFetch -> ACCESS_FAILED, not zero, but I obtained nothing from it.

THE OFFICIAL VENETO FD PAGE PUBLISHES DECREES, NOT RESULTS. I enumerated every link on regione.veneto.it/web/fitosanitario/flavescenza-dorata (HTTP 200, 52.284 bytes). The only document links are DDR_13645 14-05-2026.pdf and allegati a/b/c/d. I downloaded allegato a (HTTP 200, 1.301.187 bytes, 1 page, 200 chars - a signature sheet) and allegato c (HTTP 200, 339.903 bytes, 1 page, 4.108 chars - a three-column Prov/Comune list headed 'ZONA CUSCINETTO', e.g. BL Alano di Piave, VR Bosco Chiesanuova). These are ADMINISTRATIVE ZONE DEFINITIONS. There is not one incidence number in them.

NO 2022, 2023 OR 2025 PROCEEDINGS EXIST TO EXTEND THE SERIES. The CREA page for the combined event (crea.gov.it/web/viticoltura-e-enologia/-/bilancio-fitosanitario-2022-e-2023-della-vite-nel-nord-italia, HTTP 200, 79.218 bytes) links exactly one PDF: 'Locandina - Bilancio fitosanitario della vite nel Nord Italia - Verona 23 11 23.pdf', i.e. the event poster. No atti. The CREA notizie page (HTTP 200, 97.794 bytes) yielded no 2025 atti link. So the publication channel the hunter relies on is not even annual.

THE ONE GENUINE 3-YEAR NUMERIC GIALLUMI SERIES IN THESE DOCUMENTS IS NOT THIS CANDIDATE. Lines 344-352 of the 2024 text give 0,24% (2022), 0,45% (2023), 0,15% (2024) - but that is ALTO ADIGE, from the section 'Una retrospettiva dell'annata viticola 2024 in Alto Adige' by F. Sinn (Beratungsring), survey run by Controllo Qualita Alto Adige on 869 aziende / 415 ha / ~2,4 milioni di viti. Different province, different operator, different panel. It cannot be used to prop up the Veneto claim, and the hunter did not notice it.

THE SIGNAL IS POLICY-DRIVEN, NOT AGRONOMY-DRIVEN. The 2024 text attributes the decline to eradication compliance ('taluni piu virtuosi che praticano la bonifica ordinaria dei ceppi sintomatici con la necessaria drasticita e tempestivita') and reports 608 Ordinanze with 99%/80% remediation rates. Symptomatic-vine incidence for a phytoplasma with a multi-year latency and an insect vector under region-wide mandatory insecticide treatment measures enforcement of a Zona Delimitata, not the seasonal weather-to-disease response any infection engine would be backtested against. Weather join is not merely UNKNOWN, it is conceptually inappropriate.

DOWNSTREAM PRODUCT IS EXPLICITLY A MODEL. The Regione's own description of what happens to these data: 'Le informazioni raccolte saranno elaborate dall'Universita di Padova, che sviluppera analisi territoriali e varietali del rischio ... I modelli consentiranno inoltre di individuare le aree maggiormente [a rischio]'. The raw count is an observation, but the only elaborated output anyone publishes is a risk model - so any richer series that eventually surfaces carries a real MODELLED_RISK contamination risk.

_skeptic.notes:
ITALIAN: yes, unambiguously (Regione del Veneto / CREA Conegliano). Nothing Spanish or French touched.

THE OBSERVATION-vs-MODEL ATTACK FAILS, AND I SAY SO HONESTLY. This is not MODELLED_RISK. The variable is the count of vines carrying visible giallumi symptoms, marked by technicians walking named particelle vitate in September, with lab confirmation on 148 symptomatic samples (80% FD-positive in 2024 vs 78% in 2022). That is a real, dated, technician-recorded observation. is_really_an_observation_not_a_model = true. outcome_type INCIDENCE was correctly labelled by the hunter (% of plants affected), so no correction needed there either. The candidate dies on evidence and resolution, not on being a model.

WHAT I ACTUALLY CONFIRMED. Both hunter PDFs are real and both quotes check out verbatim: 'realizzato sul medesimo campione di 3.065 particelle vitate gia esaminate nel 2023 (2.792.208 piante esaminate di 42 varieta per complessivi 900 ettari circa su 176 Comuni)' at lines 552-553, and 'una lieve flessione della diffusione territoriale (-5,5%) ... un calo significativo dell'incidenza media dal 3-5% del 2022 ... all'1-2% rilevato nel 2024' at lines 554-556. The hunter did not fabricate anything. The panel-stability sentence is genuine and is indeed unusually strong.

WHY IT STILL CANNOT BE BACKTEST GROUND TRUTH.
(1) One year. The 2021 proceedings, which the hunter counted as the second year, contain zero percent signs anywhere in the Veneto disease section - I checked every '%' in lines 313-471 and found none. The number the hunter credited to the Veneto series ('237 vigneti', 1,17%) belongs to the Friuli-Venezia Giulia section starting at line 476. n_years_verified should have been 1 for Veneto, not 2.
(2) The 2022 comparator is not from this panel. Regione del Veneto states 2026 is the 'quarta annualita consecutiva' of systematic collection, which puts the start at 2023. The 3-5% for 2022 therefore refers to a pre-panel, unspecified assessment quoted retrospectively inside a 2024 paper.
(3) Resolution. Every published Veneto value is a BAND ('3-5%', '1-2%') or a relative change ('-5,5%'). A factor-2 interval for an entire region across 176 comuni is not a target you can score a model against. Parcel-level records exist but are held by the Servizio Fitosanitario / AVEPA and are published nowhere: dati.veneto.it has no CKAN (404 Liferay page), dati.gov.it returns success:true count:0 for 'flavescenza', and the FD page's only downloads are decree annexes that turn out to be comune lists for the zona cuscinetto.
(4) AVEPA is ACCESS_FAILED, not zero. Two curl attempts reset the connection, WebFetch got 503. If anything survives here it is a data-request lead to AVEPA / U.O. Fitosanitario, not a usable public series - and there is no evidence they release it.
(5) Even if the parcel data were obtained, the signal is wrong for the intended use. Symptomatic-vine incidence for a vector-borne phytoplasma with multi-year latency, under region-wide compulsory insecticide treatment and compulsory roguing enforced by 608 Ordinanze, measures enforcement compliance far more than season weather. The 2024 text says exactly this when it attributes the decline to growers who practise 'la bonifica ordinaria dei ceppi sintomatici con la necessaria drasticita e tempestivita'. It is a superb administrative outcome and a poor weather-driven epidemiological one.

ONE INCIDENTAL FIND WORTH PASSING UP, IN SCOPE AND ITALIAN. The same 2024 proceedings contain a cleaner three-year numeric giallumi series that is NOT this candidate and that the hunter missed: ALTO ADIGE / Sudtirol, Consorzio Vini Alto Adige with Controllo Qualita Alto Adige (SQK), coordinated by the Centro di Consulenza per la fruttiviticoltura (Beratungsring, Lana BZ), F. Sinn - 869 aziende, 415 ha (212 ha Chardonnay, 115 ha Pinot grigio, 39 ha Lagrein), circa 2,4 milioni di viti controllate, quasi 3.700 ceppi sintomatici, giving 0,24% (2022), 0,45% (2023), 0,15% (2024), plus 'per la quarta volta' implying a 2021 edition too. Those are point values, not bands. It is still an annual regional mean, still phytoplasma, still policy-confounded, and I did NOT verify it beyond this one document - but if the lane needs a giallumi series it is a strictly better-published one than Veneto. Also noted from the same 2024 volume as separately verifiable Italian vine outcomes: FVG mal dell'esca 'incidenza media supera il 6% (10% su Glera)', Trentino giallumi incidenza media 0,41% over 1.092 appezzamenti / ~350 ha, GPGV 0,57%.

VERDICT: refuted = true, survives = false. Not a fake, not a model - just one region-year of band-valued regional means, with the underlying census locked behind a service that reset my connection.
